knowledge_statements.title: Continuous Conic Relaxation Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous relaxation obtained by dropping integrality from a mixed-integer conic model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m,n\in\mathbb N\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a closed convex cone. Define
\[
v_{\mathrm{MICP}}=\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\in K,\ x_i\in\mathbb Z\text{ for every }i\in I\}
\]
and its continuous conic relaxation by
\[
v_{\mathrm{rel}}=\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\in K\}.
\]
With the convention \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\), every mixed-integer feasible point is relaxation-feasible and \(v_{\mathrm{rel}}\le v_{\mathrm{MICP}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dropping all integrality restrictions gives a continuous conic relaxation whose extended-real optimal value is a lower bound on the mixed-integer minimization value.
assumptions_latex: \(m,n\in\mathbb N\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
\(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a closed convex cone and \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
\(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_{\mathrm{rel}}\le v_{\mathrm{MICP}}\).

notation.meaning: closed convex cone defining conic feasibility

source_refs.locator: 2.13 Convex Optimization p. 76

source_witnesses.locator: 2.13 Convex Optimization p. 76

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Integer Outer-Approximation Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation-cut interface for a closed convex conic constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a constraint \(Gx+h\in K\), initialize a mixed-integer linear master with the original linear and integrality constraints and any known valid cuts. Given a master solution \(\bar x\), test \(G\bar x+h\in K\). If it fails, obtain \(w\in K^*\) satisfying \(\langle w,G\bar x+h\rangle<0\), add the valid cut \(\langle w,Gx+h\rangle\ge0\), and resolve. Stop with a conic-feasible incumbent when the prescribed bound gap is met; otherwise return the accumulated master bound and cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conic separation oracle converts each violated conic constraint into a valid linear cut for a mixed-integer master problem.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a nonempty closed convex cone.
The oracle returns a separating vector whenever its query lies outside \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Gx+h\in K\Rightarrow\langle w,Gx+h\rangle\ge0\) for every generated \(w\in K^*\).

source_refs.locator: 1.2.5 Relaxation (Successive Outer Approximation) Strategies p. 31

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2.5 Relaxation (Successive Outer Approximation) Strategies p. 31

knowledge_statements.title: Product-Cone Representation Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block representation of heterogeneous conic constraints by a finite Cartesian-product cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q,n\in\mathbb N\). For each \(j\in\{1,\ldots,q\}\), let \(m_j\in\mathbb N\), let \(K_j\subseteq\mathbb R^{m_j}\) be a closed convex cone, let \(F_j\in\mathbb R^{m_j\times n}\), and let \(g_j\in\mathbb R^{m_j}\). For \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), define \(Fx+g=(F_1x+g_1,\ldots,F_qx+g_q)\). Then
\[
Fx+g\in K_1\times\cdots\times K_q
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
F_jx+g_j\in K_j\text{ for every }j\in\{1,\ldots,q\}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
(K_1\times\cdots\times K_q)^*=K_1^*\times\cdots\times K_q^*,
\]
so primal and dual certificate data decompose into the corresponding finite blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite collection of affine conic constraints is equivalent to one product-cone constraint, and the dual of that product cone is the product of the block dual cones.
assumptions_latex: \(q,n,m_1,\ldots,m_q\in\mathbb N\).
For every \(j\), \(K_j\subseteq\mathbb R^{m_j}\) is a closed convex cone, \(F_j\in\mathbb R^{m_j\times n}\), and \(g_j\in\mathbb R^{m_j}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Fx+g\in\prod_{j=1}^qK_j\Longleftrightarrow F_jx+g_j\in K_j\) for every \(j\), and \(\left(\prod_{j=1}^qK_j\right)^*=\prod_{j=1}^qK_j^*\).

notation.meaning: dual cone of the j-th block

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Feasibility Witnesses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directly checkable feasibility certificate for a conic relaxation or mixed-integer conic system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m,n\in\mathbb N\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a closed convex cone, and let \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\). A vector \(\hat x\in\mathbb R^n\) is a primal feasibility witness for the continuous conic system exactly when \(A\hat x=b\) and \(\hat x\in K\). It is a witness for the corresponding mixed-integer conic system exactly when it additionally satisfies \(\hat x_i\in\mathbb Z\) for every \(i\in I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proposed point witnesses continuous conic feasibility when it satisfies the equations and cone constraint, and witnesses mixed-integer conic feasibility when it also satisfies every designated integrality restriction.
assumptions_latex: \(m,n\in\mathbb N\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\).
\(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a closed convex cone and \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\hat x=b\), \(\hat x\in K\), and \(\hat x_i\in\mathbb Z\) for every \(i\in I\) certify mixed-integer conic feasibility.

source_refs.locator: 2.13 Convex Optimization p. 76

source_witnesses.locator: 2.13 Convex Optimization p. 76

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Bound Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-duality certificate for a continuous conic minimization relaxation and any mixed-integer restriction of it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m,n\in\mathbb N\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a closed convex cone. Define
\[
v_P=\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\in K\}.
\]
Any \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(s\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying
\[
A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\qquad s\in K^*
\]
form a dual bound certificate with certified lower bound \(b^{\mathsf T}y\le v_P\). If a mixed-integer feasible set is obtained by imposing integrality restrictions on this continuous feasible set and has value \(v_{\mathrm{MICP}}\), then \(b^{\mathsf T}y\le v_P\le v_{\mathrm{MICP}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multiplier and dual-cone slack satisfying the displayed dual equations certify a lower bound for the continuous conic relaxation and every mixed-integer restriction of it.
assumptions_latex: \(m,n\in\mathbb N\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
\(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a closed convex cone.
The primal is a minimization problem using the displayed equality-form convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b^{\mathsf T}y\le v_P\le v_{\mathrm{MICP}}\).

notation.meaning: dual cone of K under the nonnegative-pairing convention

source_refs.locator: 2.13 Convex Optimization p. 76

source_witnesses.locator: 2.13 Convex Optimization p. 76

knowledge_statements.title: Conic Infeasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas-type sufficient certificate for infeasibility of an equality-form conic system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m,n\in\mathbb N\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a closed convex cone. Under the convention \(K^*=\{s\in\mathbb R^n:\langle s,x\rangle\ge0\text{ for every }x\in K\}\), any \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) satisfying
\[
A^{\mathsf T}y\in K^*,\qquad b^{\mathsf T}y<0
\]
is an infeasibility certificate for \(\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\). It also certifies infeasibility of every mixed-integer restriction of that conic system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multiplier whose adjoint image lies in the dual cone and whose pairing with the right-hand side is negative certifies infeasibility of the conic system and every mixed-integer restriction of it.
assumptions_latex: \(m,n\in\mathbb N\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\).
\(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a closed convex cone.
\(K^*\) uses the nonnegative-pairing convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A^{\mathsf T}y\in K^*\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y<0\Rightarrow\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ x\in K\}=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: dual cone of K under the nonnegative-pairing convention

knowledge_statements.title: Conic Recession Directions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous recession directions for an equality-form conic feasible set, with a separate lattice-preserving ray condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m,n\in\mathbb N\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a closed convex cone, and suppose \(F=\{x\in K:Ax=b\}\ne\varnothing\). A vector \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) is a recession direction of \(F\) when \(x+td\in F\) for every \(x\in F\) and every \(t\ge0\). In this setting,
\[
\operatorname{rec}(F)=K\cap\ker A.
\]
If coordinates indexed by \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) must be integral, a base point \(x^0\) with \(x_i^0\in\mathbb Z\) and a direction satisfying \(d_i\in\mathbb Z\) for every \(i\in I\) generate lattice-feasible points \(x^0+kd\) at integer parameters \(k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonempty affine slice of a closed convex cone, the recession cone is the cone intersected with the null space of the equality map. Integral increments preserve designated integer coordinates at nonnegative integer ray parameters.
assumptions_latex: \(m,n\in\mathbb N\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\).
\(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a closed convex cone.
\(F=\{x\in K:Ax=b\}\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rec}(F)=K\cap\ker A\).

source_refs.locator: 1.7 Representation of Convex Sets p. 23

source_witnesses.locator: 1.7 Representation of Convex Sets p. 23

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Unboundedness Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ray certificate for objective unboundedness in continuous or mixed-integer conic minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m,n\in\mathbb N\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a convex cone. For
\[
v_P=\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\in K\},
\]
a feasible point \(x^0\in\mathbb R^n\) and direction \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying
\[
Ax^0=b,\quad x^0\in K,\quad Ad=0,\quad d\in K,\quad c^{\mathsf T}d<0
\]
certify \(v_P=-\infty\). For a mixed-integer restriction with integer index set \(I\), the same pair certifies mixed-integer unboundedness if \(x_i^0,d_i\in\mathbb Z\) for every \(i\in I\), using the feasible sequence \(x^0+kd\) for \(k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible base point and a feasible strict-descent recession direction certify continuous conic unboundedness; integral base coordinates and increments provide a sufficient mixed-integer certificate along integer ray parameters.
assumptions_latex: \(m,n\in\mathbb N\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
\(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a convex cone.
The objective is minimization of \(c^{\mathsf T}x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_P=-\infty\).

source_refs.locator: 2.13 Convex Optimization p. 76

source_witnesses.locator: 2.13 Convex Optimization p. 76

children.title: Dual Infeasibility Link
children.top_down_role: The structural relation between primal recession evidence and dual infeasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Infeasibility Link
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implication from a primal strict-descent recession direction to infeasibility of the equality-form conic dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m,n\in\mathbb N\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a convex cone with dual \(K^*=\{s\in\mathbb R^n:\langle s,x\rangle\ge0\text{ for every }x\in K\}\). The dual-feasibility system associated with the equality-form conic minimization convention is
\[
A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\qquad y\in\mathbb R^m,\qquad s\in K^*.
\]
If \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfies \(d\in K\), \(Ad=0\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\), then this dual-feasibility system is empty. Thus the strict-descent recession direction is also a certificate of dual infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the displayed conic dual convention, a strict primal descent direction in the equality null space certifies that no dual-feasible multiplier and cone slack exist.
assumptions_latex: \(m,n\in\mathbb N\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
\(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a convex cone and \(K^*\) uses the nonnegative-pairing convention.
Primal and dual use the displayed equality-form sign convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d\in K,\ Ad=0,\ c^{\mathsf T}d<0\Rightarrow\{(y,s)\in\mathbb R^m\times K^*:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\}=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: dual cone of K under the nonnegative-pairing convention

source_refs.locator: 2.13 Convex Optimization p. 76

children.title: Unboundedness Certification Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Status regimes where recession information does not support a usable global-search certificate.

knowledge_statements.title: Unboundedness Certification Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which an apparent conic ray does not certify mixed-integer unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A vector \(d\in K\cap\ker A\) alone does not certify unboundedness. Certification also requires a feasible base point \(x^0\) and strict descent \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\). For mixed-integer unboundedness, the ray must preserve the designated lattice: it suffices that \(x_i^0\in\mathbb Z\) and \(d_i\in\mathbb Z\) for every \(i\in I\), with integer ray parameter \(t\ge0\). Consequently, unboundedness of the continuous relaxation need not imply unboundedness of the mixed-integer problem when no integer-feasible base point or lattice-preserving descent ray exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Continuous-relaxation unboundedness does not certify mixed-integer unboundedness without a feasible integer base point and a lattice-preserving descent ray.
assumptions_latex: The mixed-integer model restricts coordinates indexed by \(I\) to integers.
The continuous relaxation has equality-form conic feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_{\mathrm{rel}}=-\infty\not\Rightarrow v_{\mathrm{MICP}}=-\infty\) without an integer-feasible lattice-preserving descent ray.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated ray conditions are a plausible sufficient certification boundary, but no source is supplied for the broader mixed-integer non-implication or for the precise lattice-preservation formulation. An authoritative mixed-integer conic or mixed-integer convex optimization reference is required.

children.title: Certificate Import Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Separates imported certificate semantics from convex formulation catalogs and continuous conic solver theory.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Relaxation Requirement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissibility condition for importing certificates through a continuous convex-conic relaxation interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n,m,p\in\mathbb N\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(F\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(g\in\mathbb R^p\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) be a closed convex cone. Define
\[
R=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ Fx+g\in K\}.
\]
For an original feasible set \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), certificate import through this interface requires \(S\subseteq R\). Under this containment, every certified lower bound on \(\inf_{x\in R}c^{\mathsf T}x\) is a lower bound on \(\inf_{x\in S}c^{\mathsf T}x\), and a certificate that \(R=\varnothing\) also certifies \(S=\varnothing\). A certificate for a set not known to contain \(S\) requires an independent validity argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Import through the convex-conic interface requires a conic relaxation containing the original feasible set; its certified lower bounds and infeasibility then transfer by containment.
assumptions_latex: \(n,m,p\in\mathbb N\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(F\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(g\in\mathbb R^p\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
\(K\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) is a closed convex cone.
The original problem is a minimization problem with feasible set \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\subseteq R\Rightarrow\inf_{x\in R}c^{\mathsf T}x\le\inf_{x\in S}c^{\mathsf T}x\), and \(R=\varnothing\Rightarrow S=\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.title: Excluded Convex MICP Formulation Catalog
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The import interface validates relaxation certificates, not arbitrary MICP formulation equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let two convex MICP formulations have continuous conic relaxations \(R_1\) and \(R_2\). A certificate valid for \(R_1\) may be imported for the original feasible set \(S\) only after verifying \(S\subseteq R_1\); its validity does not follow merely because both models are described as convex MICP formulations. In particular, neither \(R_1=R_2\) nor equivalence of their integer-feasible projections is certified by this interface. Formulation classification, reformulation equivalence, and catalog completeness therefore lie outside the certificate-import claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface checks certificates for a specified relaxation; it does not classify convex MICP formulations or establish equivalence between reformulations.
assumptions_latex: \(R_1\) and \(R_2\) are continuous relaxations of stated mixed-integer conic formulations.
Certificate transfer is based on feasible-set containment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\subseteq R_1\) alone implies neither \(R_1=R_2\) nor equality of the formulations' integer-feasible projections.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The logical non-implications are plausible and the failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, but the record primarily asserts a project-specific exclusion from the certificate-import interface. No source, specification, or inspectable locator supports that scope boundary.

knowledge_statements.title: Excluded Continuous Conic Solver Theory
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of a certificate-import interface, not a claim about algorithms internal to continuous conic solvers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\) be a convex conic relaxation and let \(c\) be solver output. The import interface may check whether \(c\) satisfies specified primal-feasibility, dual-feasibility, or primal-dual gap predicates for \(R\). Acceptance certifies only the corresponding bound or feasibility assertion for \(R\). It does not certify convergence of the solver that produced \(c\), existence of an interior-point trajectory, numerical stability, or correctness of an unverified termination status. Such continuous-solver theory lies outside the interface unless independently encoded as a checkable certificate predicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Importing a verifiable conic certificate establishes its stated relaxation claim, but establishes no internal convergence or numerical-stability property of the producing solver.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) is a convex conic relaxation with explicitly checkable certificate predicates.
The imported object \(c\) is checked independently of the solver's termination declaration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance of \(c\) certifies only the checked assertion about \(R\), not the producing solver's internal theory.

notation.meaning: convex conic relaxation presented to the continuous solver

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the excluded-theory leaf, but the project-specific import semantics and exclusions have no cited specification or scholarly source.

knowledge_statements.title: Excluded General Nonconvex MINLP Catalog
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates conic-certificate importability from unrestricted nonconvex mixed-integer nonlinear modeling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{f(x,z):g_i(x,z)\le 0,\ i=1,\ldots,m,\ z\in\mathbb Z^p\}\). A general instance is outside the conic-certificate import class when no supplied node relaxation represents the relevant epigraph and constraint relaxations as convex conic systems. Merely labeling \(f\) or \(g_i\) factorable, differentiable, or globally optimizable does not produce a conic certificate. The instance enters the interface only after explicit convex conic relaxations and their verifiable bound or feasibility certificates are provided.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unrestricted nonconvex MINLP is excluded until explicit convex conic node relaxations and independently verifiable certificates are supplied.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(z\in\mathbb Z^p\), and the displayed problem is well defined.
No convex conic representation of the required node relaxations is supplied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The instance is not directly eligible for conic-certificate import.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and local scope fit, but eligibility for this particular certificate-import interface is project-specific and unsupported by any citation.

knowledge_statements.title: Conic-Representable Convex Components
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional lifted conic representation of one closed convex model component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A closed convex set \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is conic representable if there exist integers \(k,m\ge 0\), a closed convex cone \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\), matrices \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(B\in\mathbb R^{m\times k}\), and a vector \(b\in\mathbb R^m\) such that
\[C=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\exists u\in\mathbb R^k,\ Ax+Bu+b\in K\}.\]
A proper closed convex function \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is conic representable when its epigraph \(\operatorname{epi}f=\{(x,t)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R:f(x)\le t\}\) has such a representation. Linear equalities may be imposed directly or encoded using a zero-cone factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed convex set is conic representable when it is the projection of a finite-dimensional affine conic system; a proper closed convex function is conic representable when its epigraph has such a representation.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is closed and convex.
\(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is a finite-dimensional closed convex cone.
The matrices and vectors have the displayed compatible dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\) is the projection onto \(x\) of an affine conic feasible set.

notation.meaning: finite-dimensional closed convex cone, possibly a product cone
auxiliary lifting vector in the finite-dimensional space R^k

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Links Between Conic Components
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonconvexity resides in coupling relations rather than in the individual conic components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let each local component satisfy \(x_i\in C_i\), where every \(C_i\) is convex and conic representable. A nonconvex link is an additional relation \((x_1,\ldots,x_q)\in H\) whose feasible set \(H\) is nonconvex, such as an exact bilinear equality. The linked model has feasible set
\[F=\bigl(C_1\times\cdots\times C_q\bigr)\cap H.\]
Although every component admits a convex conic formulation, no convexity of \(F\) follows; global optimization must relax, partition, or otherwise certify the nonconvex linking relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex conic components can form a nonconvex model when an exact nonconvex relation couples variables belonging to different components.
assumptions_latex: Each \(C_i\) is convex and conic representable.
The coupling set \(H\) is nonconvex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The componentwise conic representations alone do not establish convexity of \(F\).

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete Activation of Conic Components
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Disjunctive representation in which integer assignments select convex conic subsystems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Z\subseteq\{0,1\}^p\) be finite. For each \(z\in Z\), suppose
\[C_z=\{x:\exists u_z,\ A_zx+B_zu_z+b_z\in K_z\},\]
where \(K_z\) is a closed convex cone. A discretely activated conic model represents
\[F=\bigcup_{z\in Z}\bigl(C_z\times\{z\}\bigr).\]
Fixing \(z=\bar z\) leaves the convex conic system defining \(C_{\bar z}\), while the unfixed mixed-integer feasible set is a finite union and need not be convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary assignments select among convex conic subsystems; fixing the assignment yields one convex component, while their union may be nonconvex.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\subseteq\{0,1\}^p\) is finite.
Each \(K_z\) is a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For fixed \(z=\bar z\), the continuous feasible region is \(C_{\bar z}\); globally it is the union \(F\).

notation.meaning: conic-representable component activated by pattern z

knowledge_statements.title: Nodewise Conic Representability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition imposed on continuous relaxations at nodes of a global mixed-integer search tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At a search node \(v\), let \(D_v\) contain the node's branching restrictions and let \(R_v\) be its continuous relaxation. Nodewise conic representability holds when there exist a closed convex cone \(K_v\), matrices \(A_v,B_v\), and a vector \(b_v\) such that
\[R_v=\{x\in D_v:\exists u,\ A_vx+B_vu+b_v\in K_v\},\]
and \(R_v\) contains every feasible point of the original nonconvex model satisfying \(D_v\). Thus optimizing over \(R_v\) gives a valid node bound whenever it is solved and certified globally.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node is conically representable when its continuous outer relaxation is an affine conic projection containing all original feasible points at that node.
assumptions_latex: \(K_v\) is a closed convex cone.
\(D_v\) encodes the restrictions imposed along the path to node \(v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_v\) is a convex conic outer relaxation and therefore supports valid certified node bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Indefinite Quadratic Objective Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization models whose objective contains a genuinely indefinite quadratic form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An indefinite quadratic objective model has objective
\[q(x)=\tfrac12 x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+\alpha,\]
where \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\) has at least one positive and at least one negative eigenvalue. Its Hessian is \(Q\), so \(q\) is neither convex nor concave on \(\mathbb R^n\). Mixed-integer restrictions or convex conic constraints may be appended, but they do not change this classification of the ambient objective; on a restricted affine hull, the reduced quadratic can nevertheless become convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The objective is an affine quadratic whose symmetric Hessian has eigenvalues of both signs, making it neither convex nor concave globally.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\).
The objective is considered on \(\mathbb R^n\) before domain restriction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\lambda_{\min}(Q)<0<\lambda_{\max}(Q)\), then \(q\) is indefinite and nonconvex.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Quadratic Constraint Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification by a nonconvex quadratic inequality function in a minimization formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A quadratic-constraint model contains an inequality
\[g(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+a^{\mathsf T}x-\beta\le 0,\]
with \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\). For a less-than-or-equal constraint, the quadratic function is convex exactly when \(Q\succeq0\); hence the constraint is classified as nonconvex quadratic when \(Q\not\succeq0\). This functional classification does not assert that every particular sublevel set is nonconvex, because additional domain restrictions or special coefficients may yield an accidentally convex feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic inequality is classified as nonconvex when its symmetric quadratic matrix is not positive semidefinite, subject to possible special-domain convexity.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\).
The inequality has the convention \(g(x)\le0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\not\succeq0\) makes \(g\) nonconvex on \(\mathbb R^n\).

knowledge_statements.title: Bilinear–Quadratic Mixed Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic models exposing cross-products as explicit bilinear auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), and define \(E=\{(i,j):1\le i<j\le n,\ Q_{ij}\ne0\}\). Introduce \(w_{ij}=x_ix_j\) for every \((i,j)\in E\). Then
\[x^{\mathsf T}Qx=\sum_{i=1}^n Q_{ii}x_i^2+2\sum_{(i,j)\in E}Q_{ij}w_{ij},\qquad w_{ij}=x_ix_j\ \text{for all }(i,j)\in E.\]
Thus the univariate squares may be retained while all nonzero cross terms are represented by bilinear graph constraints. The reformulation is exact when every displayed graph equality is enforced. Replacing those equalities by convex envelopes produces a relaxation, not an equivalent formulation unless exactness follows from additional restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every nonzero cross term of a symmetric quadratic form can be exposed using a bilinear auxiliary variable. Exact product equalities preserve the model, whereas convex envelopes generally only relax it.
assumptions_latex: \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\).
An auxiliary variable \(w_{ij}\) is introduced for every \((i,j)\in E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lifted expression equals \(x^{\mathsf T}Qx\) whenever \(w_{ij}=x_ix_j\) for every \((i,j)\in E\).

notation.meaning: index set of nonzero off-diagonal quadratic terms
auxiliary variable representing the product of coordinates i and j

knowledge_statements.title: Hidden-Convex Quadratic Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexity revealed after restricting an indefinite quadratic to an affine feasible hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+\alpha\) with \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\), and restrict \(x\) to the affine set \(x=x_0+Ny\), where the columns of \(N\) span its feasible directions. The reduced objective has Hessian \(N^{\mathsf T}QN\). Therefore
\[N^{\mathsf T}QN\succeq0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad q(x_0+Ny)\text{ is convex in }y.\]
Consequently, an ambiently indefinite quadratic is hidden-convex on that affine hull when its negative-curvature directions are excluded by the affine restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An indefinite quadratic becomes convex on an affine feasible hull exactly when its Hessian projected onto feasible directions is positive semidefinite.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\).
The affine feasible hull is parameterized as \(x=x_0+Ny\) with full-column-rank \(N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The restricted quadratic is convex if and only if \(N^{\mathsf T}QN\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: basis matrix for feasible affine directions
reduced Hessian on the affine hull

knowledge_statements.title: Binary–Continuous Product Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact linear convex-hull formulation for one bounded continuous variable multiplied by a binary variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z\in\{0,1\}\), \(\ell\le x\le u\), and \(w=zx\), where \(\ell,u\in\mathbb R\) and \(\ell\le u\). The graph is represented exactly by
\[w\ge \ell z,\quad w\le uz,\quad w\ge x-u(1-z),\quad w\le x-\ell(1-z),\quad z\in\{0,1\}.\]
If integrality is relaxed to \(0\le z\le1\), these inequalities describe the convex hull of \(\{(x,z,w):\ell\le x\le u,\ z\in\{0,1\},\ w=zx\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Four linear inequalities exactly model a bounded continuous variable times a binary variable and give its convex hull when the binary is relaxed.
assumptions_latex: \(\ell,u\in\mathbb R\) with \(\ell\le u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The four inequalities are exact for binary \(z\) and hull-defining for \(0\le z\le1\).

knowledge_statements.title: Continuous Bilinear Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: McCormick convex-hull representation for a bilinear graph over a bounded rectangle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in[\ell_x,u_x]\), \(y\in[\ell_y,u_y]\), and \(w=xy\), where all four bounds are finite. The convex hull of the bilinear graph over this rectangle is given by
\[w\ge \ell_x y+\ell_y x-\ell_x\ell_y,\qquad w\ge u_x y+u_y x-u_xu_y,\]
\[w\le u_x y+\ell_y x-u_x\ell_y,\qquad w\le \ell_x y+u_y x-\ell_xu_y.\]
These McCormick inequalities generally relax the equality \(w=xy\); their intersection, together with the variable bounds, is exactly the convex hull of the graph over the rectangle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Four McCormick inequalities, together with finite bounds on both continuous factors, give the convex hull of the bilinear graph, although they generally do not describe the graph itself.
assumptions_latex: \(\ell_x,u_x,\ell_y,u_y\in\mathbb R\), with \(\ell_x\le u_x\) and \(\ell_y\le u_y\).
\((x,y)\in[\ell_x,u_x]\times[\ell_y,u_y]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inequalities and factor bounds describe \(\operatorname{conv}\{(x,y,w):x\in[\ell_x,u_x],\ y\in[\ell_y,u_y],\ w=xy\}\).

notation.meaning: finite lower and upper bounds on the two factors

knowledge_statements.title: Multilinear Product Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines bounded multilinear terms used in factorable mixed-integer nonconvex models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be finite, let \(B\subseteq I\) index binary variables, and let \(X=\prod_{i\in I}[\ell_i,u_i]\), with \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\) for every \(i\in B\). A multilinear product model is a finite optimization model whose nonaffine terms have the form \[w_S=c_S\prod_{i\in S}x_i,\qquad S\subseteq I,\quad c_S\in\mathbb R,\] where every variable occurs with exponent at most one in each product. Products of degree two are bilinear. Repeated-variable monomials such as \(x_i^2x_j\) are not multilinear unless distinct lifted copies and linking equalities are introduced.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multilinear product model contains bounded products in which each participating variable has exponent at most one; degree-two products are bilinear.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite and \(\ell_i,u_i\in\mathbb R\) satisfy \(\ell_i\le u_i\) for every \(i\in I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w_S=c_S\prod_{i\in S}x_i\) is multilinear because each indexed variable appears at most once.

notation.meaning: Index set of factors in one product.

knowledge_statements.title: Rational Expression Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines factorable rational terms on domains excluding zero denominators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(K\) be a finite index set, and let \(p_k,q_k:X\to\mathbb R\) be finite factorable expressions for every \(k\in K\). A rational expression model contains terms \[r_k(x)=\frac{p_k(x)}{q_k(x)},\qquad k\in K,\] and has effective domain \[D=X\cap\bigcap_{k\in K}\{x\in X:q_k(x)\ne0\}.\] If integer variables are present, \(X\) may additionally impose \(x_i\in\mathbb Z\) on selected coordinates. Bounds, relaxations, and reformulations must be interpreted on \(D\), or on specified subdomains where every denominator has a known nonzero sign.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rational expression model contains finitely many quotients of factorable expressions and is defined only where every denominator is nonzero.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is finite and \(p_k,q_k:X\to\mathbb R\) for every \(k\in K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D=X\cap\bigcap_{k\in K}\{x\in X:q_k(x)\ne0\}\) is the effective domain of all rational terms.

notation.meaning: Finite index set of rational terms.
Effective domain of all rational terms.

knowledge_statements.title: Denominator-Sign Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies domains according to certified denominator bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a rational term \(p(x)/q(x)\) on \(X\), let \(L_q\le q(x)\le U_q\) for every \(x\in X\). The denominator has a positive-sign regime if \(L_q>0\), a negative-sign regime if \(U_q<0\), and a sign-indefinite regime if \(L_q\le0\le U_q\). In either fixed-sign regime, \(q\) is bounded away from zero and multiplication of an inequality by \(q(x)\) preserves or reverses its direction according to the sign. In the sign-indefinite regime, domain partitioning or an explicit exclusion of \(q(x)=0\) is required before such multiplication is logically valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified denominator bounds determine positive, negative, or sign-indefinite regimes and whether inequality cross-multiplication is valid.
assumptions_latex: \(L_q\le q(x)\le U_q\) holds for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_q>0\) or \(U_q<0\) certifies a fixed nonzero sign; \(L_q\le0\le U_q\) does not.

notation.meaning: Valid lower and upper bounds on the denominator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is mathematically standard and fits the denominator-sign leaf, but no inspectable source with a section, theorem, definition, or page locator is supplied.

children.title: Cross-Multiplied Reformulation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Validity limits affecting cross-multiplied representations of rational relations.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Multiplied Reformulation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States precisely when quotient inequalities may be cross-multiplied.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(p(x)/q(x)\le t\) on \(X\). If \(q(x)>0\) throughout \(X\), it is equivalent to \(p(x)\le t q(x)\); if \(q(x)<0\) throughout \(X\), it is equivalent to \(p(x)\ge t q(x)\). Without a fixed nonzero sign, replacing the quotient inequality by either single cross-multiplied inequality is generally invalid. For example, with \(p=1\), \(t=0\), and \(q=-1\), the quotient inequality \(-1\le0\) holds, whereas the positive-sign reformulation \(1\le0\) fails. Points satisfying \(q(x)=0\) remain outside the quotient's domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cross-multiplication is equivalent only on a fixed nonzero denominator-sign region; otherwise it can reverse inequalities or admit undefined points.
assumptions_latex: \(p,q:X\to\mathbb R\) and \(t\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A single cross-multiplied inequality is valid exactly after fixing the nonzero sign used to choose its direction.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-sign equivalences and counterexample fit this failure-boundary leaf, but the record has no cited source or locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Expression-Graph Conic Factorizations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents a factorable expression by primitive graph constraints and auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a factorable expression \(f(x)\) be represented by a finite directed acyclic graph with input nodes \(x\), primitive-operation nodes \(v_j=\phi_j(v_{\operatorname{pa}(j)})\), and output node \(v_r\). If the graph or epigraph of each primitive \(\phi_j\) admits a conic description \[(v_{\operatorname{pa}(j)},v_j,s_j)\in K_j,\qquad A_j(v_{\operatorname{pa}(j)},v_j,s_j)=b_j,\] then the conjunction of these constraints, shared-variable equalities, and \(t\ge v_r\) is an extended conic representation of \(\operatorname{epi}f\). Exactness requires each primitive description to be exact; replacing any primitive graph by a relaxation yields only an outer relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A factorable expression can be lifted along its expression graph into primitive conic constraints; the whole formulation is exact only when every primitive is exact.
assumptions_latex: The expression graph is finite and acyclic.
Each primitive graph or epigraph has the stated conic representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Projecting the lifted system onto \((x,t)\) gives \(\operatorname{epi}f\) when all primitive representations are exact.

notation.meaning: Parent nodes supplying arguments to operation node j.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied, and exact primitive epigraph descriptions do not by themselves guarantee that their conjunction exactly represents the composite epigraph; graph equality descriptions or suitable monotonicity/orientation hypotheses are needed.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Separable Nonconvexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines models whose nonconvex terms involve disjoint variable blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I_1,\ldots,I_m\) be a partition of selected variable indices, let \(x_{I_k}\in X_k\), and let \(R\) be a finite constraint index set. A model with objective \(f\) and constraints \(g_r(x)\le0\) for \(r\in R\) has block-separable nonconvexity under this partition if \[f(x)=f_0(x)+\sum_{k=1}^m f_k(x_{I_k})\] and \[g_r(x)=g_{r0}(x)+\sum_{k=1}^m g_{rk}(x_{I_k}),\qquad r\in R,\] where \(f_0\) and every \(g_{r0}\) are convex or affine, and every nonconvex summand depends on only one block. Any additional coupling constraints must be convex or affine; otherwise the nonconvexity is not block-separable under this partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonconvexity is block-separable when every nonconvex term depends on one disjoint variable block and all cross-block coupling is convex or affine.

children.title: Network-Structured Nonconvex Models
children.top_down_role: Nonconvex models whose coupling follows an underlying network topology.

knowledge_statements.title: Network-Structured Nonconvex Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents local node and edge nonlinearities coupled by network incidence equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(N,A)\) be a finite directed graph, let \(B\) be its node-arc incidence matrix, let \(x_a\in\mathbb R\) be an arc variable for each \(a\in A\), and let \(y_i\in\mathbb R^{p_i}\) be a node variable for each \(i\in N\). For functions \(f_i:\mathbb R^{p_i}\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) and \(h_a:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), local sets \(C_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{p_i+|\delta(i)|}\), arc sets \(D_a\subseteq\mathbb R\), and a balance vector \(d\), a network-structured model has the lifted form \[\inf_{x,y}\left\{\sum_{i\in N}f_i(y_i)+\sum_{a\in A}h_a(x_a):Bx=d,\ (y_i,x_{\delta(i)})\in C_i\ \forall i\in N,\ x_a\in D_a\ \forall a\in A\right\},\] possibly with selected integer coordinates. Nonconvexity is network-local when every nonconvex function or set involves one node, one arc, or variables incident to one node; the affine balance equation \(Bx=d\) supplies the global coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A network-structured model combines node- or arc-local nonconvex functions and sets with global flow-balance equations defined by the incidence matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(N,A)\) is a finite directed graph.
\(B\) is the node-arc incidence matrix of \(G\).
\(\delta(i)\) denotes the arcs incident to node \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All nonconvex factors are local to nodes or arcs, while \(Bx=d\) provides affine network coupling.

knowledge_statements.title: Chordal Decomposition Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the clique interface for sparse positive-semidefinite completion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be chordal with maximal cliques \(C_1,igots,C_m\), and let \(X\) be a symmetric partial matrix whose specified entries are the diagonal and edges of \(G\). Then \(X\) has a positive-semidefinite completion if and only if \[X[C_k,C_k]\succeq0igqquadigl(k=1,igots,migr).\] In a lifted optimization model using separate clique matrices \(X^k\), equality of entries shared by intersecting cliques is additionally imposed. Thus a sparse semidefinite interface replaces one completion constraint by clique-level positive-semidefinite constraints plus overlap consistency. For nonchordal sparsity, a chordal extension is required before applying this interface.

children.title: Coupling-Induced Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural regimes where global coupling defeats sparse or network decomposition.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((0,0,0,-1,-1,-1)\) satisfies every separate bilinear McCormick envelope but is outside the joint convex hull.
review_flags: Exact coupling-boundary source is missing; candidate uses a concrete inconsistent-cycle witness.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of edgewise convexification on a three-cycle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the three-cycle product set \(S=\{(x,w):x\in[-1,1]^3,\ w_{12}=x_1x_2,\ w_{23}=x_2x_3,\ w_{31}=x_3x_1\}\). Applying the exact four-inequality McCormick envelope separately to each edge admits \(x_1=x_2=x_3=0\) and \(w_{12}=w_{23}=w_{31}=-1\). This point is not in \(\operatorname{conv}(S)\): equality \(w_{ij}=-1\) in any convex combination forces \(x_i x_j=-1\) almost surely, while the three simultaneous equalities would imply \((x_1x_2)(x_2x_3)(x_3x_1)=-1\), contradicting \(x_1^2x_2^2x_3^2\ge 0\). Thus exact edge envelopes need not describe the joint convex hull when products are coupled around a cycle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separate exact envelopes for the edges of a product cycle can admit lifted points that violate an unavoidable joint consistency relation.
knowledge_statements.title: Coupling-Induced Failure Boundaries

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_B=\{(x,w):x\in B,\ w=f(x)\}\). The box-domain convexification of this graph is \[\operatorname{conv}(G_B)=\{(x,w):x\in B,\ \operatorname{vex}_B f(x)\le w\le\operatorname{cav}_B f(x)\},\] where \(\operatorname{vex}_B f\) is the greatest convex underestimator of \(f\) on \(B\), and \(\operatorname{cav}_B f\) is the least concave overestimator. Consequently, replacing \(w=f(x)\) by these envelope inequalities gives the strongest closed convex relaxation obtainable without introducing information beyond the restricted graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact box, exact graph convexification is the region between the factor's convex and concave envelopes restricted to that box.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be a finite index set, let \(w=xy\) with \(x\in[\ell_x,u_x]\) and \(y\in[\ell_y,u_y]\), and let the intervals \([a_k,b_k]\), \(k\in K\), cover \([\ell_x,u_x]\). Introduce \(\delta_k\ge 0\) and \((x_k,y_k,w_k)\in\mathbb R^3\) for each \(k\in K\), and impose \(\sum_{k\in K}\delta_k=1\), \(x=\sum_{k\in K}x_k\), \(y=\sum_{k\in K}y_k\), and \(w=\sum_{k\in K}w_k\), together with \(a_k\delta_k\le x_k\le b_k\delta_k\) and \(\ell_y\delta_k\le y_k\le u_y\delta_k\). For every \(k\in K\), impose \(w_k\ge a_k y_k+\ell_y x_k-a_k\ell_y\delta_k\), \(w_k\ge b_k y_k+u_y x_k-b_k u_y\delta_k\), \(w_k\le b_k y_k+\ell_y x_k-b_k\ell_y\delta_k\), and \(w_k\le a_k y_k+u_y x_k-a_k u_y\delta_k\). The projection of this continuous extended formulation is \(\operatorname{conv}\!\left(\bigcup_{k\in K}\{(x,y,xy):x\in[a_k,b_k],\ y\in[\ell_y,u_y]\}\right)\). Requiring \(\delta_k\in\{0,1\}\) selects one cellwise McCormick hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded bilinear graph is split into interval-specific graphs. Scaled McCormick inequalities and continuous selector weights give the convex hull of their union; binary selectors instead select one cellwise McCormick hull.

The intervals \([a_k,b_k]\), \(k\in K\), cover \([\ell_x,u_x]\).

knowledge_statements.title: Piecewise Factor Convexification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partition-based convexification of factorable expressions on bounded boxes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=\{(x,z):x\in B,\ z=\phi(x)\}\), where \(B\) is a bounded box, and let \(\mathcal P\) be a finite partition of \(B\) into boxes \(B_s\). Replacing each restricted graph \(G_s=G\cap(B_s\times\mathbb R)\) by a convex relaxation \(R_s\supseteq\operatorname{conv}(G_s)\), and taking a valid disjunctive convex-hull formulation of \(\bigcup_sR_s\), yields a convex relaxation of \(G\). If a refinement \(\mathcal P'\) uses exact cellwise convex hulls, its projected relaxation is contained in that from \(\mathcal P\); hence refinement cannot weaken the relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexify a factor separately on partition cells and combine the cells disjunctively. Exact cellwise hulls become at least as strong when the partition is refined.
assumptions_latex: \(B\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a bounded box.
\(\mathcal P'\) refines \(\mathcal P\) for the monotonicity conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The construction is valid, and exact cellwise convexification satisfies \(R(\mathcal P')\subseteq R(\mathcal P)\).

knowledge_statements.title: alphaBB Underestimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal alphaBB convex underestimator on a bounded box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\subset\mathbb R^n\), let \(f\) be twice continuously differentiable on an open neighborhood of \(B\), and choose \(\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n)\in\mathbb R_+^n\) such that \(\nabla^2 f(x)+2\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\succeq0\) for every \(x\in B\). Define \[f_{\alpha}(x)=f(x)-\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(x_i-\ell_i)(u_i-x_i).\] Then \(f_{\alpha}\) is convex on \(B\), satisfies \(f_{\alpha}(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in B\), and agrees with \(f\) at every vertex of \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative separable quadratic correction chosen to offset negative Hessian curvature gives a convex lower estimator that agrees with the original function at every vertex of the box.
assumptions_latex: \(B=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\) is a nonempty bounded box.
\(f\) is twice continuously differentiable on an open neighborhood of \(B\).
\(\alpha\in\mathbb R_+^n\) and \(\nabla^2 f(x)+2\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\succeq0\) for every \(x\in B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The function \(f_{\alpha}\) is convex on \(B\), satisfies \(f_{\alpha}\le f\) on \(B\), and equals \(f\) at every vertex of \(B\).

knowledge_statements.title: Difference-of-Convex Underestimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex underestimation obtained from a DC decomposition and an affine majorant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) be convex and let \(f=g-h\) on \(C\), where \(g\) and \(h\) are convex. If an affine function \(a\) satisfies \(a(x)\ge h(x)\) for every \(x\in C\), then
\[
 \underline f(x)=g(x)-a(x)
\]
is convex and obeys \(\underline f(x)\le f(x)\) on \(C\). Thus any verifiable affine majorant of the subtracted convex component generates a convex underestimator. In particular, on a simplex, the affine interpolant of convex \(h\) through the vertices majorizes \(h\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a DC function, subtracting an affine upper bound of the subtracted convex component yields a convex lower bound of the original function.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is convex.
\(f=g-h\) with convex \(g,h:C\to\mathbb R\).
\(a\) is affine and satisfies \(a\ge h\) on \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The function \(\underline f=g-a\) is convex and satisfies \(\underline f\le f\) on \(C\).

knowledge_statements.title: Interval-Based Convex Underestimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Isotropic convex underestimator derived from an interval-certified Hessian bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:|x_i-c_i|\le r_i,\ i=1,\ldots,n\}\), where \(c\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(r\in\mathbb R_+^n\), and let \(f\) be twice continuously differentiable on an open neighborhood of \(B\). Suppose interval Hessian analysis certifies \(\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2 f(x))\ge-2\gamma\) for every \(x\in B\), where \(\gamma\ge0\). Then \[\underline f(x)=f(x)+\gamma\lVert x-c\rVert_2^2-\gamma\lVert r\rVert_2^2\] is convex on \(B\) and satisfies \(\underline f(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An interval-certified lower bound on Hessian eigenvalues determines an isotropic quadratic correction that gives a convex lower estimator on the box.

\(f\) is twice continuously differentiable on an open neighborhood of \(B\).
Interval analysis certifies \(\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2 f(x))\ge-2\gamma\) for every \(x\in B\), with \(\gamma\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The function \(\underline f\) is convex on \(B\) and satisfies \(\underline f(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in B\).

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic SOC Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rotated-cone lift of a convex quadratic epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), let \(R\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) satisfy \(Q=R^{\mathsf T}R\), and define \[\mathcal Q_r^{m+2}=\{(u,v,z)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^m:u\ge0,\ v\ge0,\ 2uv\ge\lVert z\rVert_2^2\}.\] For \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(t\in\mathbb R\), the convex quadratic epigraph has the exact lifted representation \[x^{\mathsf T}Qx\le t\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad(t,\tfrac12,Rx)\in\mathcal Q_r^{m+2}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factoring a positive-semidefinite quadratic form converts its epigraph exactly into a dimension-compatible rotated second-order cone constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\).
\(R\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(Q=R^{\mathsf T}R\).
\(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(t\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality \(x^{\mathsf T}Qx\le t\) is equivalent to \((t,\tfrac12,Rx)\in\mathcal Q_r^{m+2}\).

notation.meaning: rotated second-order cone with an m-dimensional vector component

knowledge_statements.title: Rotated-Cone Product Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rotated-cone representation of a nonnegative hyperbolic product inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\ge0\), \(y\ge0\), and \(w\in\mathbb R\), the hyperbolic product inequality
\[
 w^2\le xy
\]
has the exact rotated-cone representation
\[
 (x,y,\sqrt2\,w)\in\mathcal Q_r^3,
 \qquad
 \mathcal Q_r^3=\{(u,v,z):u\ge0,\ v\ge0,\ 2uv\ge z^2\}.
\]
Consequently, whenever a nonconvex formulation implies a valid inequality of the form \(w^2\le xy\) with nonnegative factors, retaining this cone constraint gives a convex product relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A squared variable bounded by a product of nonnegative variables is exactly representable by a three-dimensional rotated second-order cone.
assumptions_latex: \(x\ge0\) and \(y\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The conditions \(w^2\le xy\), \(x,y\ge0\) are equivalent to \((x,y,\sqrt2w)\in\mathcal Q_r^3\).

knowledge_statements.title: Aggregated SOC Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-cone aggregation of several convex quadratic epigraph inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r_i(x)=A_ix+b_i\) and introduce scalars \(t_i\). The aggregated relaxation of the separate inequalities \(\|r_i(x)\|_2^2\le t_i\), \(i=1,\ldots,p\), is
\[
 \sum_{i=1}^p\|r_i(x)\|_2^2\le\sum_{i=1}^pt_i,
\]
equivalently
\[
 \left(\sum_i t_i,\tfrac12,(r_1(x),\ldots,r_p(x))\right)\in\mathcal Q_r.
\]
It uses one rotated SOC constraint and is valid for every point satisfying all separate inequalities, but it permits compensation between violated and slack component inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Several quadratic epigraph constraints may be summed into one rotated cone, reducing constraint count while allowing slack in one component to offset violation in another.
assumptions_latex: Each residual \(r_i(x)=A_ix+b_i\) is affine.
The intended separate constraints satisfy \(t_i\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All disaggregated inequalities imply the displayed aggregated SOC inequality.

knowledge_statements.title: Disaggregated SOC Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise rotated-cone representation of separable quadratic epigraph inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r_i(x)=A_ix+b_i\). The disaggregated SOC relaxation retains, for every \(i=1,\ldots,p\),
\[
 \|r_i(x)\|_2^2\le t_i
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 (t_i,\tfrac12,r_i(x))\in\mathcal Q_r.
\]
The feasible set is the intersection of these \(p\) cones. Summing the component inequalities recovers the corresponding aggregated SOC constraint, so disaggregation is at least as strong whenever the individual variables \(t_i\) and their linking restrictions are retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keeping one rotated cone per quadratic component prevents cross-component compensation and implies the corresponding single aggregated cone.
assumptions_latex: Each residual \(r_i(x)=A_ix+b_i\) is affine.
Each \(t_i\) is retained explicitly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The disaggregated feasible set is contained in the associated aggregated SOC feasible set.

knowledge_statements.title: Aggregation Strength Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dominance and strictness of disaggregated versus aggregated SOC systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For affine residuals \(r_i(x)\), define \(D=\{(x,t):\|r_i(x)\|_2^2\le t_i\ \forall i\}\) and \(A=\{(x,t):\sum_i\|r_i(x)\|_2^2\le\sum_it_i\}\). Then \(D\subseteq A\). The inclusion can be strict: with two scalar residuals having squared values \((2,0)\) and \((t_1,t_2)=(1,1)\), the aggregate inequality \(2\le2\) holds, whereas the first disaggregated inequality \(2\le1\) fails. Aggregation therefore reduces cone count but may weaken the relaxation through cross-component compensation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Disaggregated cones dominate their sum. Aggregation is smaller but can be strictly weaker because excess slack in one component can cover another component's violation.
assumptions_latex: The same affine residuals and epigraph variables are used in both systems.
No additional constraints force equivalence between component and aggregate inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: One has \(D\subseteq A\), and the inclusion is strict in general.

knowledge_statements.title: SOC Strengthening with Linear Envelopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intersection of SOC constraints with bound-derived linear product envelopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_i\in[\ell_i,u_i]\), \(x_j\in[\ell_j,u_j]\), and let \(W_{ij}\) represent \(x_ix_j\) in an SOC relaxation. Add the four McCormick inequalities
\[
\begin{aligned}
W_{ij}&\ge \ell_i x_j+\ell_jx_i-\ell_i\ell_j, &
W_{ij}&\ge u_i x_j+u_jx_i-u_iu_j,\\
W_{ij}&\le u_i x_j+\ell_jx_i-u_i\ell_j, &
W_{ij}&\le \ell_i x_j+u_jx_i-\ell_i u_j.
\end{aligned}
\]
Every exact product point satisfies these inequalities. Hence intersecting them with any valid SOC outer relaxation preserves validity and produces a feasible set contained in the original SOC relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: McCormick inequalities derived from variable bounds can be intersected with an SOC relaxation, preserving all exact product points while never weakening the relaxation.
assumptions_latex: Both factors have finite lower and upper bounds.
\(W_{ij}=x_ix_j\) at every exact feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The SOC-plus-envelope relaxation is valid and is contained in the unstrengthened SOC relaxation.

notation.meaning: lifted surrogate for the product of factors i and j

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted Product-Matrix Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semidefinite outer relaxation obtained by lifting all quadratic products.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), introduce \(X\in\mathbb S^n\) to represent \(xx^{\mathsf T}\). Exact lifting satisfies
\[
Y=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}1\\x\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}1\\x\end{pmatrix}^{\mathsf T},
\qquad \operatorname{rank}(Y)=1.
\]
Dropping the rank constraint while imposing \(Y\succeq0\), equivalently \(X-xx^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\), yields an SDP outer relaxation. Every quadratic expression \(x^{\mathsf T}Qx+q^{\mathsf T}x+c\) is then replaced by the affine lifted expression \(\langle Q,X\rangle+q^{\mathsf T}x+c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lift products into a symmetric matrix, linearize quadratic expressions, and drop the matrix's rank-one requirement while retaining positive semidefiniteness.
assumptions_latex: Quadratic terms involve a finite-dimensional vector \(x\in\mathbb R^n\).
The leading entry of \(Y\) is fixed to one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constraint \(Y\succeq0\) with linearized quadratic expressions is a convex outer relaxation of the exact product-matrix formulation.

notation.meaning: lifted surrogate for the product matrix xx-transpose
trace inner product replacing the quadratic form

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Relaxation Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard lifted rank-one representation and its semidefinite relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a vector variable \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), introduce \(X\in\mathbb S^n\) and \(Y=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\). The exact lifted product relation \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) is equivalent to \(Y\succeq0\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(Y)=1\). Dropping only the rank constraint gives the convex relaxation \(Y\succeq0\), equivalently \(X-xx^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\). Thus every exact lifted point is feasible for the relaxation, while matrices of rank greater than one constitute its relaxation gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted quadratic model is exact when its moment matrix is positive semidefinite and rank one; deleting rank one yields the standard SDP relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb R^n\)
\(X\in\mathbb S^n\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\iff Y\succeq0,\ \operatorname{rank}(Y)=1\), and relaxing rank yields \(Y\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: real symmetric matrices of order n

children.title: Sparse SDP Relaxations

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse SDP Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: PSD relaxation retaining only matrix entries used by a sparse quadratic model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) contain every diagonal pair and every index pair appearing in the objective or constraints of a lifted quadratic model. A sparse SDP relaxation retains the partial matrix \(X_E=(X_{ij})_{ij\in E}\) and imposes membership in the projected PSD cone \(\mathcal S_+^n(E)=\{X_E:\exists Z\in\mathbb S_+^n,\ Z_{ij}=X_{ij}\text{ for all }ij\in E\}\). Linear lifted constraints use only entries in \(E\). This formulation has the same projection as the corresponding dense SDP whenever the projected cone is represented exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparse SDP keeps only matrix entries used by the model and requires that the resulting partial matrix admit a positive-semidefinite completion.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) contains all specified lifted entries
\(X_E\) is symmetric on its specified indices
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X_E\in\mathcal S_+^n(E)\) exactly characterizes projections of dense PSD-feasible matrices.

notation.meaning: partial symmetric matrix supported on E
projection of the positive-semidefinite cone onto E

children.title: Chordal SDP Relaxations

knowledge_statements.title: Chordal SDP Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-semidefinite completion theorem for chordal aggregate sparsity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be chordal, include every loop, and have maximal cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\). A partial symmetric matrix \(X_E\) has a positive-semidefinite completion if and only if every fully specified principal clique matrix is positive semidefinite: \[X_E\in\mathcal S_+^n(E)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad X[C_k,C_k]\succeq0\ \text{ for }k=1,\ldots,m.\] Consequently, a sparse PSD constraint on chordal support can be represented by smaller clique PSD constraints, with shared entries identified across intersecting cliques.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For chordal sparsity, a partial matrix has a PSD completion exactly when every maximal-clique principal submatrix is PSD and overlaps share the same entries.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is chordal and contains all loops
\(C_1,\ldots,C_m\) are the maximal cliques of \(G\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X_E\in\mathcal S_+^n(E)\iff X[C_k,C_k]\succeq0\) for every \(k\).

notation.meaning: a maximal clique of the chordal graph

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is the chordal PSD-completion theorem and requires a specific theorem or section citation before candidate review can pass.

children.title: Clique-Consistency Coupling
children.top_down_role: Consistency requirements linking overlapping clique-level semidefinite blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Clique-Consistency Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Entrywise compatibility condition for independently modeled clique matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be chordal with maximal cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\), and let \(T\) be a clique tree for these cliques. For each \(k\), let \(X^{(k)}\in\mathbb S^{|C_k|}\) be a local matrix. Clique consistency requires \[X^{(k)}[C_k\cap C_\ell,C_k\cap C_\ell]=X^{(\ell)}[C_k\cap C_\ell,C_k\cap C_\ell].\] It suffices to impose this equality for every clique-tree edge \(\{k,\ell\}\in E(T)\). The resulting local matrices define a single partial symmetric matrix on the union of their supports; without these equalities, independently feasible clique matrices need not represent a common lifted point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local clique matrices must agree entrywise on overlaps. For a clique tree, enforcing agreement along its edges ensures consistency across every clique intersection.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is chordal
\(C_1,\ldots,C_m\) are its maximal cliques
\(T\) is a clique tree for the maximal cliques
\(X^{(k)}\in\mathbb S^{|C_k|}\) for \(k=1,\ldots,m\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Adjacent-clique overlap equalities along \(E(T)\) imply consistency on every clique intersection.

notation.meaning: local symmetric matrix for clique k

children.title: Nonchordal Sparsity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural limitations arising from nonchordal patterns or costly chordal extensions.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonchordal Sparsity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Four-cycle showing that local PSD edge tests do not ensure PSD completion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) be the chordless cycle on vertices \(1,2,3,4\). Specify \(X_{ii}=1\), \(X_{12}=X_{23}=X_{34}=1\), and \(X_{41}=-1\). Every specified edge principal matrix is positive semidefinite because it equals either \(\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}\) or \(\begin{pmatrix}1&-1\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}\). Nevertheless no PSD completion exists: a Gram representation would force the first three equalities to identify all four unit vectors, contradicting their required inner product \(-1\) on edge \(41\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a chordless four-cycle, all edge submatrices can be PSD while the partial matrix has no PSD completion.
assumptions_latex: \(G=C_4\) has no chord
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All clique submatrices are PSD, but \(X_E\notin\mathcal S_+^4(E)\).

notation.meaning: the chordless cycle on four vertices

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The four-cycle counterexample is coherent and fits the failure-boundary container, but no inspectable source is provided.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Decomposed SDP Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decomposition of a large PSD condition into coupled blockwise PSD constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_1,\ldots,B_m\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) be index sets whose block supports cover all lifted entries used by a model. A block-decomposed SDP replaces the projected dense condition \(X\succeq0\) by local variables \(X^{(k)}\in\mathbb S_+^{|B_k|}\) and the equalities \(X^{(k)}_{ij}=X^{(\ell)}_{ij}\) whenever \(i,j\in B_k\cap B_\ell\). This is an exact representation of the projected dense PSD cone when the blocks are the maximal cliques of a chordal sparsity graph. For arbitrary blocks, the local system is generally an outer relaxation of the projected dense PSD cone and becomes exact only when the associated PSD-completion conditions are sufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block SDP uses smaller PSD matrices coupled on overlaps. Chordal maximal-clique blocks exactly represent the projected dense PSD cone; arbitrary blocks generally give an outer relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(B_1,\ldots,B_m\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\)
\(\bigcup_{k=1}^m B_k\times B_k\) covers every required lifted entry
Shared block entries are identified
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Chordal maximal-clique blocks give an exact projected PSD representation; otherwise the displayed local system is generally an outer relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Closed-Perspective Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed convex perspective for an on/off convex epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, and convex, with recession function \(f^\infty\). Define its closed perspective by \[\widetilde f(x,z)=\begin{cases}z f(x/z),&z>0,\\f^\infty(x),&z=0,\\+\infty,&z<0.\end{cases}\] Let \(S_0=\{(0,0,t):t\ge0\}\) and \(S_1=\{(x,1,t):x\in\mathbb R^n,\ t\ge f(x)\}\). Then \[\operatorname{clconv}(S_0\cup S_1)=\{(x,z,t):x\in\mathbb R^n,\ 0\le z\le1,\ t\ge\widetilde f(x,z)\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed perspective represents the closed convex hull of a convex epigraph switched off at zero and active at one.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper, closed, and convex
\(f^\infty\) is the recession function of \(f\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{clconv}(S_0\cup S_1)=\{(x,z,t):x\in\mathbb R^n,\ 0\le z\le1,\ t\ge\widetilde f(x,z)\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Perspective-Cut Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Supporting-hyperplane inequalities for a differentiable perspective epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n	o\mathbb R\) be differentiable and convex, and define \(g(x,z)=z f(x/z)\) for \(z>0\). For every anchor \( ar x\in\mathbb R^n\), convexity yields the valid perspective cut \[t\ge f( ar x)z+
abla f( ar x)^{\mathsf T}(x- ar x z)=
abla f( ar x)^{\mathsf T}x+ igl(f( ar x)-
abla f( ar x)^{\mathsf T} ar x igr)z.\] The intersection of all such cuts is the epigraph of the closed perspective when supporting hyperplanes recover the closed convex function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each tangent to a convex function homogenizes into a linear cut valid for its perspective epigraph; all tangents recover the closed perspective.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable and convex
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t\ge\nabla f(\bar x)^{\mathsf T}x+(f(\bar x)-\nabla f(\bar x)^{\mathsf T}\bar x)z\) is valid for every \(\bar x\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The tangent perspective cut is mathematically standard and the representation kind fits, but no source supports the validity and recovery claims.

knowledge_statements.title: Conic Disjunctive-Hull Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended conic formulation of the convex hull of finitely many conic sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(i=1,\ldots,m\), let \(S_i=\{x:A_i x-b_i\in K_i\}\), where each \(K_i\) is a closed convex cone. Introduce \(x^i\) and weights \(\lambda_i\ge0\). The conic disjunctive-hull formulation is \[x=\sum_{i=1}^m x^i,\qquad \sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i=1,\qquad A_i x^i-b_i\lambda_i\in K_i\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).\] Its projection contains \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_i S_i)\), and equals its closure under the standard recession-compatibility and closedness conditions for homogenized disjunctive formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Disjunct-specific conic variables and convex weights form an extended relaxation whose projection is the closed convex hull under suitable recession and closedness conditions.
assumptions_latex: \(K_i\) is a closed convex cone for every \(i\)
\(S_i=\{x:A_i x-b_i\in K_i\}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed extended system projects to \(\operatorname{clconv}(\bigcup_{i=1}^m S_i)\) under hull-closedness conditions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact projected-hull conclusion depends on recession and closedness hypotheses that are only described generically. A specific source is needed to determine and support the correct theorem version.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Perspective Strengthening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perspective strengthening applied only to separable terms controlled by activation variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(F(x)=h(x)+\sum_{j\in J} f_j(x_j)\), where each \(f_j\) is proper closed convex and \(x_j=0\) whenever the associated indicator \(z_j=0\). Replacing only the selected terms by their closed perspectives gives \[t\ge h(x)+\sum_{j\in P}\widetilde f_j(x_j,z_j)+\sum_{j\in J\setminus P}f_j(x_j),\qquad P\subseteq J.\] This inequality is valid for all integer-feasible activated points. For relaxed indicators, it dominates the unperspectivized epigraph whenever \(f_j(0)=0\) and \(0\le z_j\le1\), but may be weaker than full perspective convexification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perspectivizing only selected activated convex terms preserves validity and strengthens their continuous relaxation, though it can be weaker than full convexification.
assumptions_latex: \(f_j\) is proper, closed, convex, and \(f_j(0)=0\)
\(x_j=0\) whenever \(z_j=0\)
\(0\le z_j\le1\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The partial-perspective inequality is valid and dominates the corresponding unperspectivized selected terms.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The partial-perspective validity and dominance property is plausible under the stated normalization, but no citation or locator supports the specialized claim.

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Conic Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conic lower bound obtained by dualizing selected constraints of a minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(p^*=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ g(x)=0,\ h(x)\in-K\}\), where \(K\) is a closed convex cone and \(X\) retains the constraints not dualized. For \(y\in K^*\) and unrestricted \(\lambda\), define \[L(x,\lambda,y)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}g(x)+\langle y,h(x)\rangle,\qquad q(\lambda,y)=\inf_{x\in X}L(x,\lambda,y).\] Then \(q(\lambda,y)\le p^*\), and the Lagrangian conic relaxation bound is \(d^*=\sup_{\lambda,\,y\in K^*}q(\lambda,y)\le p^*\). Equality requires an applicable strong-duality condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual multipliers from the dual cone produce globally valid lower bounds; maximizing these bounds gives the Lagrangian conic dual value.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone
\(y\in K^*\) and \(\lambda\) is unrestricted
The primal problem is a minimization problem
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^*=\sup_{\lambda,\,y\in K^*}q(\lambda,y)\le p^*\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The multiplier signs correctly yield weak-duality lower bounds for the stated cone convention, and the duality kind fits, but the record lacks evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Decomposed Conic Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-cone relaxation assembled from coupled local conic blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let global variables \(x\) induce block variables \(x^{(k)}=P_kx\), and suppose block \(k\) has affine conic condition \(A_kx^{(k)}-b_k\in K_k\). A block-decomposed conic relaxation introduces independent \(x^{(k)}\), imposes \(A_kx^{(k)}-b_k\in K_k\) for every \(k\), and couples duplicated coordinates by \(R_kx^{(k)}=R_\ell x^{(\ell)}\) on prescribed overlaps. It is exact for the original conic feasible set when these consistency equations ensure existence of a common \(x\); omitting necessary coupling enlarges the feasible set and therefore yields a lower bound for minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local conic blocks are solved with overlap equalities; complete consistency is exact, while omitted coupling gives a relaxation for minimization.
assumptions_latex: \(K_k\) is a closed convex cone for each block
\(x^{(k)}=P_kx\) describes the intended global-to-local maps
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Complete overlap consistency recovers a common global point; weakened consistency produces a conic outer relaxation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The block-product-cone representation and effect of omitted consistency constraints are appropriate, but no inspectable source supports the exactness statement.

assumptions_latex: The node relaxation regions satisfy \(R_0\supseteq R_1\supseteq\cdots\supseteq R_m\supseteq F\).
Each tier minimizes the same objective \(f\) and returns a valid lower bound or a certified failure status.
An incumbent upper bound \(U\) is available for pruning.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_0\le L_1\le\cdots\le L_m\le \inf_{x\in F}f(x)\), and any tier with \(L_k\ge U\) certifies node pruning.

notation.meaning: lower bound returned at tier k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite nested cascade for minimization at one branch-and-bound node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a node domain, solve the conic relaxations \(R_0,R_1,\ldots,R_m\) in increasing order of strength. At tier \(k\), set \(L_k:=\inf\{f(x):x\in R_k\}\). Stop and prune when \(L_k\ge U\); stop and retain the node when a prescribed resource limit is reached; otherwise advance to tier \(k+1\). Because \(R_{k+1}\subseteq R_k\) and \(F\subseteq R_k\), every successfully computed value is a valid node lower bound and the sequence is monotone: \[L_0\le L_1\le\cdots\le L_m\le\inf_{x\in F}f(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve nested conic relaxations from cheapest to strongest. Their lower bounds increase monotonically, and any bound reaching the incumbent value certifies pruning.
knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Tier Conic Relaxation Cascades

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nested-set bound ordering and pruning rule are mathematically coherent, and algorithm is the appropriate content kind. No cited source supports the conic cascade or its stopping/status contract; the unlinked inventory does not satisfy the evidence requirement.

children.title: Moment–SOS Relaxation Interface
