children.title: Integer-Outer Nested Search
children.top_down_role: Nested architectures placing discrete search outside spatial global optimization.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer-Outer Nested Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested search with an outer integer tree and inner global continuous optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{f(x,z):(x,z)\in F,\ z\in\mathbb Z^p\}\), initialize an outer branch-and-bound tree over integer regions \(Z_N\) and incumbent \(U=+\infty\). At each outer node, invoke an inner spatial global solver on \(F_N=F\cap(X\times Z_N)\) until it returns a certified lower bound \(L_N\), certified infeasibility, or a feasible point. Prune when infeasibility is certified or \(L_N\geq U-\varepsilon\); otherwise update \(U\) and branch the integer region. Stop when all outer nodes are pruned or resolved, and return the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An outer integer tree delegates each node’s nonconvex continuous optimization to a certified inner spatial solver.
assumptions_latex: Each inner solve produces globally valid bounds for its complete outer-node region.
Outer branching children cover the parent integer region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exhausting the outer tree yields a globally \(\varepsilon\)-optimal incumbent.

notation.meaning: integer assignments represented by outer node N

source_refs.locator: 3.12 The GOP in a Branch and Bound Framework p. 114

source_witnesses.locator: 3.12 The GOP in a Branch and Bound Framework p. 114

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but the cited GOP branch-and-bound section does not establish this integer-outer architecture. It is also unclear whether an outer region may contain multiple integer assignments, in which case the described inner problem is not purely continuous.

children.title: Spatial-Outer Nested Search
children.top_down_role: Nested architectures placing spatial partitioning outside discrete subsearches.

knowledge_statements.title: Spatial-Outer Nested Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested search with outer spatial partitioning and inner discrete global optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize an outer spatial tree with continuous box \(X_0\), incumbent \(U=+\infty\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon\). For each outer box \(X_N\), invoke an inner mixed-integer solver on a relaxation valid over all \(x\in X_N\), obtaining a certified lower bound \(L_N\), certified infeasibility, and possibly a feasible point. Prune when infeasibility is certified or \(L_N\geq U-\varepsilon\); otherwise update \(U\) and bisect a continuous interval. The children must cover \(X_N\). Stop when every active box is pruned or has bound at least \(U-\varepsilon\), and return the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An outer spatial tree partitions continuous domains while an inner mixed-integer solver bounds every discrete choice within each box.
assumptions_latex: The root continuous domain is bounded.
Inner bounds apply to every integer choice feasible in the outer box.
Spatial children cover their parent box.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Upon termination, the incumbent is globally \(\varepsilon\)-optimal.

notation.meaning: continuous box at outer node N

source_refs.locator: 3.12 The GOP in a Branch and Bound Framework p. 114

source_witnesses.locator: 3.12 The GOP in a Branch and Bound Framework p. 114

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but the generic GOP citation does not support this spatial-outer mixed-integer architecture or its exact termination claim. A direct source and explicit treatment of unresolved inner solves are needed.

children.title: Cross-Level Bound Transfer
children.top_down_role: Transfer of qualified bounds between the outer and inner search levels.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Level Bound Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity conditions for transferring bounds between outer and inner nested-search levels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let outer node \(N\) have feasible set \(F_N\), and let \(K_N\) be an index set of inner regions \(F_{Nk}\) satisfying \(F_N\subseteq\bigcup_{k\in K_N}F_{Nk}\). If \(L_{Nk}\leq\inf_{y\in F_{Nk}}f(y)\) for every \(k\in K_N\), then \(L_N:=\inf_{k\in K_N}L_{Nk}\) is a valid lower bound for \(N\). If a child feasible set \(F_M\) satisfies \(F_M\subseteq F_N\), every bound \(L_N\leq\inf_{y\in F_N}f(y)\) is also valid for \(F_M\). Without such containment, validity on \(F_N\) alone does not imply validity on \(F_M\); any transfer then requires an independent validity argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounds for regions covering an outer node combine by their infimum. A parent bound is automatically valid on a subset, while transfer without containment requires a separate validity argument.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
\(K_N\) is nonempty, and the indexed inner regions cover the outer feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stated covering and feasible-set-inclusion relations are sufficient for valid cross-level lower-bound transfer.

notation.meaning: valid lower bound for inner region k

children.title: Nesting Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Architectural regimes where nested search loses useful coordination or certification.

knowledge_statements.title: Nesting Failure Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mechanisms by which nested discrete–spatial search loses global validity or finite resolution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nested search cannot certify global \(\varepsilon\)-optimality if any outer node \(N\) is pruned using an inner value \(\widehat L_N\) that exceeds \(\inf_{y\in F_N}f(y)\), if inner subregions fail to cover \(F_N\), or if transferred cuts exclude a point of the receiving node’s feasible set. It may also fail to terminate finitely when unresolved inner calls can recur indefinitely without certified bounds, exhaustive branching, or a positive progress rule. In these regimes the outer exhaustion test does not imply that every omitted feasible point has objective at least \(U-\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invalid inner bounds, incomplete coverage, nonlocal cuts, or endlessly unresolved inner calls break the global certificate supplied by outer-tree exhaustion.
assumptions_latex: The nested method claims global optimality from pruning and exhaustion of outer nodes.
\(U\) is the incumbent value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under any listed failure mechanism, outer-tree exhaustion alone is not a global \(\varepsilon\)-optimality certificate.

notation.meaning: complete feasible set represented by outer node N

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits and the listed mechanisms are plausible, but no source supports this particular taxonomy or the finite-resolution condition.

knowledge_statements.title: Outer-Approximation-Managed Spatial Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Master outer approximation coordinating globally valid spatial relaxations for nonconvex MICP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a mixed-integer master containing the original variable bounds and globally valid outer-approximation cuts, with incumbent \(U=+\infty\). Solve the master to obtain a lower bound \(L\) and candidate region or assignment. Invoke a spatial global subsolver on that candidate; add only cuts valid on the master region, update \(U\) from verified feasible points, and spatially branch whenever the relaxation gap cannot be closed by valid cuts. Repeat until the master is infeasible or \(U-L\leq\varepsilon\). Return the incumbent together with the master lower bound and the retained cut-validity domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed-integer outer-approximation master schedules spatial solves, accepts only region-valid cuts, and terminates when its certified lower bound meets the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: Every master cut is valid throughout its declared domain.
Spatial branching covers the unresolved candidate region.
Subsolver infeasibility and bounds are certified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination with \(U-L\leq\varepsilon\), the incumbent is globally \(\varepsilon\)-optimal.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but no source supports the proposed master/subsolver architecture, region-local cut handling, or the claim that the reported master value remains a global lower bound throughout spatial refinement.

children.title: Branch-Cut-Price Architecture
children.top_down_role: Global-search architectures combining tree exploration, cut generation, and dynamic columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Branch-Cut-Price Architecture
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integrated branch-and-bound with separation and dynamically generated variables or columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a restricted master at the root, an incumbent \(U=+\infty\), and an active-node list. At node \(N\), repeatedly solve the restricted relaxation, separate violated globally or locally valid cuts, and call a pricing oracle for omitted columns. Declare the node bound \(L_N\) certified only when separation requirements are satisfied and pricing certifies that no admissible omitted column has negative reduced cost. Prune when infeasibility is certified or \(L_N\geq U-\varepsilon\); otherwise update \(U\) from feasible solutions and branch with exhaustive children. Stop when all nodes are pruned, and return the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch-cut-price alternates relaxation, cut separation, and column pricing; a node bound is final only after qualified separation and pricing.
assumptions_latex: The relaxation is a minimization master problem.
Cuts and branching constraints retain their declared validity.
Branching children cover the parent feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If every pruned-node bound is certified, tree exhaustion establishes global \(\varepsilon\)-optimality.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits. The description is plausible for linear branch-cut-price, but its use as an architecture for nonconvex MICP and its separation-completeness requirements need direct authoritative support.

children.title: Column-Generation Interface
children.top_down_role: The interface between restricted conic relaxations and dynamically generated columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Column-Generation Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricted-master and pricing relation for a nodewise linear relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(N\), let the full master relaxation be \(\min\{\sum_{j\in J_N}c_j\lambda_j:A_N\lambda=b_N,\ \lambda\geq0\}\), and let a nonempty set \(J_N^R\subseteq J_N\) define its restricted master. Let \(\pi_N\) be an optimal dual solution of the restricted master, and define \(\bar c_j:=c_j-\pi_N^{\mathsf T}a_j\) for every \(j\in J_N\). Pricing searches the complete set \(J_N\setminus J_N^R\) for a column with \(\bar c_j<0\). If pricing certifies \(\bar c_j\geq0\) for every \(j\in J_N\), then \(\pi_N\) is feasible for the full-master dual and the restricted- and full-master optimal values are equal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The restricted master supplies an optimal dual vector. Pricing either adds a negative-reduced-cost omitted column or certifies full-dual feasibility, in which case the restricted and full relaxation values coincide.
assumptions_latex: The full and restricted node masters are feasible linear programs with finite optimal values.
\(\pi_N\) is an optimal restricted-master dual solution.
The pricing oracle ranges over every node-admissible omitted column.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Certified nonnegative reduced costs for all node-admissible columns make the restricted-master optimum exact for the full node relaxation.

notation.meaning: columns currently present at node N
column j of the master constraint matrix

children.title: Pricing Oracle Qualification
children.top_down_role: Certification requirements for pricing information used within global search.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing Oracle Qualification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate condition permitting a pricing result to close a node relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization restricted master with dual vector \(\pi_N\), a pricing oracle is qualified to certify node closure only if it returns a verifiable number \(\ell_N\) satisfying \(\ell_N\leq\min_{j\in J_N}(c_j-\pi_N^{\mathsf T}a_j)\) over the complete node-admissible column set \(J_N\). Closure is valid when \(\ell_N\geq-\tau\), where \(\tau\geq0\) is the declared pricing tolerance. A heuristic failure to find a negative-reduced-cost column, or optimization over a strict unaccounted subset of \(J_N\), does not satisfy this qualification condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing closes a node only with a verifiable lower bound on minimum reduced cost over every admissible column; heuristic non-discovery is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: The restricted-master dual vector is feasible for its stated dual constraints.
Reduced costs use the same scaling and tolerance convention as the master.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only \(\ell_N\geq-\tau\) from complete certified pricing qualifies the no-improving-column claim.

notation.meaning: complete set of columns admissible at node N
certified lower bound on minimum reduced cost

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits and the lower-bound implication is mathematically plausible. A direct source is required to establish what closure within pricing tolerance certifies and how that tolerance propagates to the node and global gaps.

children.title: Global-Bound Preservation
children.top_down_role: Conditions governing preservation of valid global bounds under restricted-column relaxations.

knowledge_statements.title: Global-Bound Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verifiable conditions under which branch-cut-price node bounds remain globally valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every active or pruned node \(N\), a value \(L_N\) certifies a global lower bound only if the node relaxation contains every feasible solution represented by \(N\), all retained cuts are valid on that node, and pricing qualification covers every admissible omitted column. If the active nodes cover all feasible solutions not dominated by the verified incumbent \(U\), then \(L=\min_{N\in\mathcal A}L_N\) is a global lower bound. Consequently, \(U-L\leq\varepsilon\) is a verifiable global \(\varepsilon\)-optimality certificate; an empty active set certifies optimality when all prior pruning tests were valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global bounds survive branch-cut-price only when node relaxations cover feasible solutions, cuts are valid, pricing is complete, and active nodes cover all unresolved solutions.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
\(U\) is the objective of a verified feasible solution.
Every prior node removal used a certified pruning rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pair \((U,L)\) certifies global gap at most \(\varepsilon\) whenever \(U-L\leq\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: certified lower bound at node N

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits, but the integrated branch-cut-price validity conditions lack a citation. The minimum over active nodes is undefined when the active set is empty, so that case must be treated separately in any sourced final formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Static Root Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Root-built relaxation reused throughout a spatial branch-and-bound tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the root domain be \(D^0\), let \(F(D)\) denote the original feasible set restricted to \(D\subseteq D^0\), and construct once a tractable set \(R^0\) satisfying \(F(D^0)\subseteq R^0\). At every descendant node \(D\), use \(R_{\mathrm{stat}}(D)=R^0\cap D\) and compute \[L_{\mathrm{stat}}(D)=\inf\{c(x):x\in R_{\mathrm{stat}}(D)\}.\] Then \(F(D)\subseteq R_{\mathrm{stat}}(D)\), so \(L_{\mathrm{stat}}(D)\leq\inf\{c(x):x\in F(D)\}\). The relaxation is static because its inequalities and envelope parameters are not rebuilt using descendant bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A root relaxation intersected with each descendant domain remains a valid lower-bounding relaxation, although it does not exploit tighter descendant bounds when constructing envelopes.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subseteq D^0\).
\(F(D^0)\subseteq R^0\).
The problem is a minimization problem with objective \(c\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_{\mathrm{stat}}(D)\leq\inf\{c(x):x\in F(D)\}\).

notation.meaning: Original feasible set within node domain D.
Static-relaxation lower bound at node D.

source_refs.locator: 8.3 Global Optimization Algorithm p. 276

source_witnesses.locator: 8.3 Global Optimization Algorithm p. 276

knowledge_statements.title: Domain-Adaptive Node Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node relaxation rebuilt from the current spatial domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every node domain \(D\subseteq D^0\), construct a tractable set \(R(D)\) using the current variable bounds and require \(F(D)\subseteq R(D)\). Define \[L(D)=\inf\{c(x):x\in R(D)\}.\] Then \(L(D)\leq\inf\{c(x):x\in F(D)\}\). For a factor \(w=xy\), for example, replacing root bounds by the bounds valid on \(D\) in its convex-envelope inequalities preserves validity and can strictly shrink the relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rebuilding valid envelopes with current node bounds yields a sound lower bound and can tighten the relaxation relative to root-bound envelopes.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subseteq D^0\).
\(F(D)\subseteq R(D)\).
Every bound used to construct \(R(D)\) is valid throughout \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(D)\leq\inf\{c(x):x\in F(D)\}\).

source_refs.locator: 8.3 Global Optimization Algorithm p. 276

source_witnesses.locator: 8.3 Global Optimization Algorithm p. 276

knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Tier Relaxation Cascades
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential solution of increasingly strong valid node relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a node domain \(D\), incumbent value \(U\), and relaxation tiers \(R_1(D),\ldots,R_m(D)\) satisfying \(F(D)\subseteq R_k(D)\) for every \(k\). Initialize \(k=1\). Solve tier \(k\) to obtain \(L_k(D)=\inf\{c(x):x\in R_k(D)\}\). If it proves infeasibility or \(L_k(D)\geq U\), prune the node. Otherwise, if a prescribed escalation test holds and \(k<m\), set \(k\leftarrow k+1\) and repeat. If no escalation occurs, return the current bound and relaxation solution for branching or incumbent processing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve valid relaxations from cheap to strong; prune at any conclusive tier, escalate when prescribed, and otherwise pass the current result to branching.
assumptions_latex: \(F(D)\subseteq R_k(D)\) for \(k=1,\ldots,m\).
Every tier is solved sufficiently to establish its reported bound or infeasibility.
\(U\) is the objective value of a feasible incumbent or \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_k(D)\) is a valid node lower bound at every reached tier \(k\).

children.title: Relaxation Switching Policies
children.top_down_role: Policies for selecting a different relaxation family at a search node.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Switching Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State-dependent selection among valid relaxation tiers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s(D)\) contain the node depth, relaxation history, bound gaps, violation measures, and computational budget. Given a deterministic policy \(\pi\) with \(\pi(s(D))\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), select tier \(k=\pi(s(D))\), solve \(R_k(D)\), and update the state with its bound and cost. The policy may switch tiers between nodes or after a solve, but pruning is permitted only from a tier satisfying \(F(D)\subseteq R_k(D)\). If no selected tier proves pruning, return the last valid bound and a branching decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A switching policy maps observable node state to a relaxation tier; switching affects effort and strength, while validity of the selected tier preserves sound pruning.
assumptions_latex: \(\pi(s)\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) for every admissible state \(s\).
Each tier used for pruning satisfies \(F(D)\subseteq R_k(D)\).
Tier bounds are computed with certified solver status.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_k(D)\geq U\) implies that node \(D\) may be pruned whenever \(k=\pi(s(D))\).
review_flags: No supplied source locator identifies a formal relaxation-switching policy.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the container and its pruning condition is sound, but the formal state-dependent switching policy has no supporting source locator.

children.title: Relaxation Escalation Triggers
children.top_down_role: Structural or performance signals supporting movement to a stronger relaxation tier.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Escalation Triggers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checkable predicates that request a stronger relaxation tier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After solving tier \(k<m\) at node \(D\), define the escalation predicate \[T_k(D)=\mathbf{1}\!\left\{g_k(D)>	au_g\ \lor\ v_k(D)>	au_v\ \lor\ q_k(D)<\tau_q\right\}.\] Here \(g_k(D)=(U-L_k(D))/\max\{1,|U|\}\) is the relative incumbent gap, \(v_k(D)\) is a nonnegative measure of violation of omitted nonconvex relations, and \(q_k(D)\) is a predicted bound-improvement-per-unit-cost score. Escalate from tier \(k\) to tier \(k+1\) exactly when \(T_k(D)=1\) and the remaining budget permits the stronger solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Escalation occurs when the incumbent gap or omitted-relation violation is large, or predicted relaxation efficiency is poor, subject to available computational budget.
assumptions_latex: \(U<+\infty\) when the relative gap trigger is evaluated.
\(\tau_g,\tau_v\geq0\) and \(\tau_q\in\mathbb{R}\) are fixed policy thresholds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_k(D)=1\) is the formal request to solve tier \(k+1\).

notation.meaning: Relative incumbent gap at tier k.
Violation of relations omitted by tier k.

review_flags: Trigger formula is a precise policy template, but no supplied source supports this particular combination of criteria.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is internally defined, but the particular disjunctive trigger formula, thresholds, and interpretation of the efficiency score are unsupported policy choices.

children.title: Tier-Transition Validity
children.top_down_role: Validity considerations when bounds or cuts move between relaxation tiers.

knowledge_statements.title: Tier-Transition Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and bound monotonicity under strengthening transitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization node \(D\), suppose adjacent tiers satisfy \[F(D)\subseteq R_{k+1}(D)\subseteq R_k(D).\] With \(L_j(D)=\inf\{c(x):x\in R_j(D)\}\), the transition from tier \(k\) to tier \(k+1\) preserves every feasible point and satisfies \[L_k(D)\leq L_{k+1}(D)\leq\inf\{c(x):x\in F(D)\}.\] Consequently, infeasibility of \(R_{k+1}(D)\) or the test \(L_{k+1}(D)\geq U\) is a valid pruning certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Moving to a nested stronger relaxation preserves all feasible points, cannot weaken the lower bound, and maintains sound infeasibility and incumbent-bound pruning.
assumptions_latex: \(F(D)\subseteq R_{k+1}(D)\subseteq R_k(D)\).
The objective \(c\) is minimized.
\(U\) is the value of a feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_k(D)\leq L_{k+1}(D)\leq\inf\{c(x):x\in F(D)\}\).

notation.meaning: Original feasible set at node D.

children.title: Escalation Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes where stronger relaxations do not justify their computational or numerical cost.

knowledge_statements.title: Escalation Failure Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mechanisms that destroy validity or prevent useful strengthening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An escalation scheme can fail in three distinct regimes. First, if some selected tier omits a feasible point, so \(F(D)\nsubseteq R_k(D)\), its bound may exceed the true node optimum and pruning can be incorrect. Second, if all tiers have a persistent gap, meaning \(\sup_k L_k(D)<\inf\{c(x):x\in F(D)\}\), escalation alone cannot close that node gap. Third, if the trigger never selects a required stronger tier on an infinite descendant sequence, weak bounds may persist despite valid tiers. Thus validity, sufficient approximation strength, and trigger fairness are separate requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Escalation fails through invalid tiers, a persistent relaxation gap across all tiers, or trigger starvation that indefinitely avoids necessary stronger relaxations.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem on node domain \(D\).
The escalation mechanism selects from a prescribed family \(\{R_k(D)\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(D)\nsubseteq R_k(D)\), a persistent tier gap, or trigger starvation defeats respectively soundness, gap closure, or effective escalation.
review_flags: No supplied source locator treats escalation failure regimes as a formal classification.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, but the three-regime classification and trigger-fairness requirement are nontrivial and have no supporting citation.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Domain Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spatial partition by splitting a bounded variable domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a node with box domain \(D=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\), select an index \(j\) with \(\ell_j<u_j\) and a split point \(s\in(\ell_j,u_j)\). Create children \[D^-=D\cap\{x:x_j\leq s\},\qquad D^+=D\cap\{x:x_j\geq s\}.\] Rebuild or restrict valid relaxations on both children and insert every nonpruned child into the search queue. Because \(D=D^-\cup D^+\), the split loses no feasible point; overlap at \(x_j=s\) is harmless.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split one bounded variable interval into two covering child domains, solve valid child relaxations, and continue with every child not certified prunable.
assumptions_latex: \(D=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\).
\(\ell_j<s<u_j\).
Child relaxations contain their respective original feasible sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Factor-Violation Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spatial branching driven by violated lifted factor equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a relaxation solution be \((\bar x,\bar w)\) for lifted equations \(w_r=\phi_r(x)ishhookleft r=1,\ldots,p\). Compute \(v_r=|\bar w_r-\phi_r(\bar x)|\) and choose an index \(r^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_r v_r\). Select a bounded argument \(x_j\) of \(\phi_{r^*}\) with positive interval width, choose \(s\in(\ell_j,u_j)\), and create the two covering children \(x_j\leq s\) and \(x_j\geq s\). Reconstruct the factor relaxation in each child. Stop factor-based branching when every \(v_r\) is within its prescribed feasibility tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose the most violated lifted factor equation, split a bounded argument of that factor, rebuild child envelopes, and stop when all factor violations satisfy tolerance.
assumptions_latex: Each lifted equation is \(w_r=\phi_r(x)\).
At least one argument of the selected factor has finite positive width.
The two child domains cover the parent domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(D)=F(D^-)\cup F(D^+)\), with branching targeted at \(r^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_r v_r\).

notation.meaning: Violation of lifted factor equation r.

review_flags: No supplied locator supports this specific factor-violation branching rule.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the specific maximum-factor-violation rule, and the lifted-equation display contains the corrupted text “ishhookleft” where the index qualification should appear. Source-backed correction is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Violation Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spatial branching targeted by violation of a lifted rank-one relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a relaxation uses \(X\) for \(xx^{\mathsf T}\) and returns \((\bar x,\bar X)\). Form \(M=\bar X-\bar x\bar x^{\mathsf T}\), choose a unit eigenvector \(v\) associated with \(\lambda_{\max}(M)>\varepsilon\), and set \(s=v^{\mathsf T}\bar x\). Branch into \[D^-=D\cap\{x:v^{\mathsf T}x\leq s\},\qquad D^+=D\cap\{x:v^{\mathsf T}x\geq s\}.\] Rebuild valid lifted relaxations on both children. If \(\lambda_{\max}(M)\leq\varepsilon\), this rank-violation rule does not branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use the leading eigenvector of the lifted rank-one residual to define two covering spatial halfspaces, then rebuild valid relaxations on both children.
assumptions_latex: The lifted model requires \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\).
\(M=\bar X-\bar x\bar x^{\mathsf T}\) is symmetric.
The child halfspaces are intersected with the parent domain \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D=D^-\cup D^+\), so the eigenvector split preserves every parent-feasible point.

notation.meaning: Residual of the lifted rank-one relation.

review_flags: No supplied source locator supports the stated eigenvector branching construction.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The halfspace split covers the parent domain, but no citation supports using the leading eigenvector of this residual and splitting at its relaxed-solution projection as the stated rank-violation branching algorithm.

knowledge_statements.title: Disjunctive Conic Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branching on a finite union of conic representable sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the unresolved nonconvex restriction at node \(D\) be \(z(x)\in\bigcup_{q=1}^Q C_q\), where each \(C_q\) has a tractable conic representation. Create child \(q\) by imposing \(z(x)\in C_q\) and retaining all parent restrictions. Construct a valid conic relaxation for each child, discard certified infeasible children, and place the others in the search queue. Since \[D\cap z^{-1}\!\left(\bigcup_{q=1}^Q C_q\right)=\bigcup_{q=1}^Q\left(D\cap z^{-1}(C_q)\right),\] the disjunction covers exactly the parent points satisfying the restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Create one child for each conic term of a finite disjunction; their union exactly covers the parent points satisfying the nonconvex restriction.
assumptions_latex: \(Q<\infty\).
The restriction is exactly \(z(x)\in\bigcup_{q=1}^Q C_q\).
Each child admits a valid tractable conic relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(D)=\bigcup_{q=1}^Q F(D\cap z^{-1}(C_q))\).
review_flags: No supplied locator specifically addresses finite disjunctive conic branching.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-disjunction identity is sound and the algorithm fits the leaf, but the disjunctive conic branching construction lacks a supporting source locator.

children.title: Reliability Branching
children.top_down_role: Branching choices governed by the reliability of accumulated candidate statistics.

knowledge_statements.title: Reliability Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branching that combines strong-branch probes with qualified pseudocosts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each branching candidate \(j\), maintain directional pseudocost means \(p_j^-,p_j^+\) and observation counts \(n_j^-,n_j^+\). Given reliability threshold \(\eta\), obtain predicted child-bound gains from pseudocosts when \(n_j^-,n_j^+\geq\eta\); otherwise temporarily solve both child relaxations and use their observed gains, updating the means and counts. Score candidate \(j\) by \[S_j=(1-\mu)\min\{\Delta_j^-,\Delta_j^+\}+\mu\max\{\Delta_j^-,\Delta_j^+\},\] where \(0\leq\mu\leq1\). Branch on a maximizer of \(S_j\) and retain the two covering children.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use strong-branch probes until both directional pseudocosts are sufficiently observed, then use their predictions; select the candidate with the best balanced gain score.
assumptions_latex: \(\eta\in\mathbb{N}\) is positive and \(0\leq\mu\leq1\).
Each candidate defines two children covering the parent domain.
Observed gains come from valid child lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(j^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_j S_j\) is selected, using probes for unqualified directions and pseudocosts for qualified directions.

notation.meaning: Directional pseudocost means for candidate j.

review_flags: No supplied source locator covers reliability branching, pseudocost qualification, or the stated score.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm has the expected reliability-branching structure, but the directional qualification rule, probing procedure, and parameterized gain score require an authoritative citation.

children.title: Hybrid Branching
children.top_down_role: Branching selectors combining multiple discrete or spatial scoring families.

assumptions_latex: The node relaxation is a minimization problem over a bounded mixed-integer spatial domain.
Strong-branching scores and pseudocost estimates are available for eligible branching candidates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned disjunction covers the parent domain and therefore preserves every globally feasible solution.

notation.meaning: reliability count for candidate and direction

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports this hybrid branching rule.
Exact score aggregation and tie-breaking conventions are solver-dependent.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A reliability-style hybrid of strong branching and pseudocost branching for spatial branch-and-cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given eligible candidates \(J\), directions \(\sigma\in\{-,+\}\), observation counts \(n_j^\sigma\), pseudocost predictions \(p_j^\sigma\), and qualification threshold \(N_{\mathrm{rel}}\), initialize scores for every \(j\in J\). If \(n_j^-<N_{\mathrm{rel}}\) or \(n_j^+<N_{\mathrm{rel}}\), tentatively solve both child relaxations and use their nonnegative bound improvements \(s_j^-\) and \(s_j^+\); otherwise set \(s_j^\sigma=p_j^\sigma\). Select a maximizer of a fixed monotone aggregation \(\Phi(s_j^-,s_j^+)\), create its two exhaustive children, update the corresponding pseudocost statistics from completed child solves, and stop when no branchable candidate remains or the node is fathomed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use strong branching for insufficiently sampled candidates and pseudocost scores for qualified candidates, then branch on the best aggregated two-child score.
knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Branching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the Hybrid Branching leaf, but no citation supports the qualification rule, score aggregation, or pseudocost-update convention.

children.title: Pseudocost Qualification
children.top_down_role: Reliability regimes for pseudocost information used in branching decisions.

assumptions_latex: Each directional pseudocost observation is computed from a finite positive branching displacement and a valid child-bound improvement.
Observations are maintained separately for the two branching directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Qualification authorizes pseudocost prediction only in directions having the prescribed minimum number of valid observations.

notation.meaning: number of valid observations for candidate and direction

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports pseudocost qualification.
Qualification thresholds and admissible observation filters vary across implementations.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional reliability predicate for pseudocost use in mixed discrete-spatial branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For candidate \(j\) and direction \(\sigma\in\{-,+\}\), let valid observations be pairs \((\delta_{jk}^\sigma,\Delta_{jk}^\sigma)\) satisfying \(0<\delta_{jk}^\sigma<\infty\) and \(0\leq\Delta_{jk}^\sigma<\infty\). Define \(n_j^\sigma\) as their number and, when \(n_j^\sigma>0\), define \(p_j^\sigma=(n_j^\sigma)^{-1}\sum_k\Delta_{jk}^\sigma/\delta_{jk}^\sigma\). Direction \((j,\sigma)\) is pseudocost-qualified at threshold \(N_{\mathrm{rel}}\in\mathbb N\) exactly when \(n_j^\sigma\geq N_{\mathrm{rel}}\). Candidate \(j\) is fully qualified exactly when both directions are qualified; otherwise every unqualified direction requires an external estimate, such as strong branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A directional pseudocost is qualified only after enough valid bound-improvement-per-displacement observations; full candidate qualification requires both directions.
knowledge_statements.title: Pseudocost Qualification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the chosen observation filter or qualification convention. Moreover, the threshold must be explicitly positive; if natural numbers include zero, a direction could qualify while its pseudocost remains undefined.

children.title: Regime-Dependent Branching Selection
children.top_down_role: Problem or node regimes favoring different hybrid branching components.

assumptions_latex: Every available branching rule produces an exhaustive child disjunction.
The regime classifier uses only information available at the current node.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Regime-dependent selection preserves completeness while allowing different scoring costs and information sources across search regimes.
review_flags: No supplied locator identifies a formal regime-selection policy.
The intended regimes may be solver-specific and require source confirmation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Policy-level selection among reliable branching rules as node information and search phase change.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\) be the set of node states and \(\mathcal B\) a finite family of branching rules, each mapping an applicable state \(z\in Z\) to children whose domains cover the parent domain. A regime-dependent selector is a map \(\pi:Z\to\mathcal B\) satisfying applicability: \(\pi(z)\) may be chosen only when its required statistics and candidate class are available at \(z\). The selected rule may depend on depth, remaining discrete and spatial candidates, pseudocost qualification, and allotted scoring effort. Since each selected disjunction is exhaustive, changing \(\pi(z)\) across regimes changes search efficiency but does not remove a parent-feasible point solely through branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose an applicable branching rule from node-dependent regimes; exhaustive child coverage preserves correctness even though scoring effort and information vary.
knowledge_statements.title: Regime-Dependent Branching Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The policy-level kind fits the leaf, but the regime policy has no source. Exhaustive child coverage preserves feasible-point coverage locally; it alone does not establish completeness of the entire search procedure.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq R\subseteq[l,u]\), and suppose a dual-feasible multiplier vector \(\lambda\) certifies \(q_\lambda(x)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in R\). Given a valid objective cutoff \(\bar f\), every retained point \(x\in F\) with \(f(x)\leq\bar f\) must satisfy \(q_\lambda(x)\leq\bar f\). Consequently, any coordinate interval \(I\subseteq[l_j,u_j]\) for which \(\inf\{q_\lambda(x):x\in R,\ x_j\in I\}>\bar f\) contains no retained feasible value and may be deleted. The dual-feasible vector together with the certified infimum is a checkable range-reduction certificate.

Then \(f(x)\leq\bar f\) implies \(x_j\leq l_j+(\bar f-L)/r_j\). Thus \(u_j\) may be replaced by \(\min\{u_j,l_j+(\bar f-L)/r_j\}\). Symmetrically, if the certificate implies \(f(x)\geq L+(-r_j)(u_j-x_j)\) with \(r_j<0\), then \(l_j\) may be replaced by \(\max\{l_j,u_j-(\bar f-L)/(-r_j)\}\), with certified rounding and integrality adjustments.
