knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq B^0\) be the node-feasible points satisfying the valid objective cutoff. For \(k=1,\ldots,m\), assume \(T_k\) is contracting and sound: whenever \(S\subseteq B\), one has \(S\subseteq T_k(B)\subseteq B\). Starting from \(B^0\), apply any finite schedule \(B^{t+1}=T_{k_t}(B^t)\). Induction gives \(S\subseteq B^t\subseteq B^0\) for every \(t\), so combining feasibility, cutoff, reduced-cost, and optimization-based tightening cannot invalidate a retained solution. If iteration terminates at \(B^\star\) with \(T_k(B^\star)=B^\star\) for every scheduled \(k\), then \(B^\star\) is a common fixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sound tightening operators may be composed in any finite schedule; all retained solutions survive, and convergence yields a box stable under every scheduled operator.
knowledge_statements.title: Combined Tightening Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Basic Concepts of Global Optimization p. 33

children.title: Invalid-Inference Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on propagation when bounds, dual information, or relaxation qualifications are unreliable.

assumptions_latex: The problem is minimization on \([0,1]\) with objective \(f(x)=x\).
The valid cutoff is \(\bar f=1\), and the exact lower bound and reduced cost are \(L=0\) and \(r=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing a certified lower bound by an unsupported larger value can make reduced-cost propagation delete cutoff-feasible points.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly documents this failure example.
The example is elementary but requires an explicit supporting source under the evidence contract.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete boundary showing why reduced-cost inference requires a valid dual lower-bound certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{x:0\leq x\leq1\}\) with cutoff \(\bar f=1\). The valid relaxation data are \(L=0\) and lower-bound reduced cost \(r=1\), yielding \(x\leq0+(\bar f-L)/r=1\). If one substitutes an unsupported value \(\widetilde L=a\) with \(0<a<1\), the same formula yields the invalid restriction \(x\leq1-a\). Yet every \(x\in(1-a,1]\) is feasible and satisfies \(f(x)\leq\bar f\). Thus reduced-cost propagation is sound only when the lower bound, reduced-cost inequality, sign convention, and cutoff refer to the same valid relaxation certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Using an unsupported lower bound in a reduced-cost formula can exclude feasible cutoff-satisfying points, even for minimizing one variable on an interval.
knowledge_statements.title: Invalid-Inference Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The elementary counterexample is mathematically correct and fits a failure-boundary leaf, but the record supplies neither a citation nor an explicit standard-field rationale as required by the evidence contract.

assumptions_latex: The relaxation \(R\) contains the original feasible set \(F\).
The certificate proves validity of an inequality for every point in \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A violated certificate-backed inequality is a valid separating cut for the relaxation point and preserves all original-feasible points.
review_flags: No supplied locator specifically addresses certificate-cut separation.
The admissible certificate families depend on the nonconvex formulation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation whose cut validity is independently justified by a verifiable certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and let \(\bar x\in R\) be the point to separate. A certificate-cut pair consists of finite data \(c\) and an inequality \(a(c)^Tx\leq b(c)\) such that a deterministic verifier confirms \(a(c)^Tx\leq b(c)\) for every \(x\in F\). If \(a(c)^T\bar x>b(c)+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{sep}}\), add the inequality to obtain \(R'=R\cap\{x:a(c)^Tx\leq b(c)\}\). The verifier establishes \(F\subseteq R'\), while the strict violation establishes \(\bar x\notin R'\). If verification or violation fails, the candidate inequality is not accepted as a certificate cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Verify a candidate inequality is valid for all feasible points, then add it only when it strictly separates the current relaxation point.
knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-Cut Separation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic separation logic is sound, but no source identifies the intended certificate family for nonconvex MICP. The separation tolerance is also used without an explicit domain or nonnegativity condition.

children.title: Envelope Cut Separation
children.top_down_role: Separation of cuts induced by convex or concave envelopes over bounded domains.

assumptions_latex: A bilinear term is represented by \(w=xy\) on finite bounds \(x\in[l_x,u_x]\) and \(y\in[l_y,u_y]\).
The separation point satisfies the variable bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every added McCormick envelope inequality is valid for the bilinear graph and excludes the relaxation point when violated beyond tolerance.

notation.meaning: auxiliary variable representing the bilinear product

review_flags: The broad global-optimization locator must be checked for the exact four McCormick inequalities.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of violated McCormick envelope facets for a bounded bilinear graph.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Basic Concepts of Global Optimization p. 33

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(w=xy\) over \([l_x,u_x]\times[l_y,u_y]\), evaluate at \((\bar x,\bar y,\bar w)\) the four inequalities \(w\geq l_xy+l_yx-l_xl_y\), \(w\geq u_xy+u_yx-u_xu_y\), \(w\leq u_xy+l_yx-u_xl_y\), and \(w\leq l_xy+u_yx-l_xu_y\). Add every inequality violated by more than \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{sep}}\), optionally retaining only a maximally violated member under a fixed normalization. Stop when none is violated. Each inequality is valid for every bounded point satisfying \(w=xy\); therefore every accepted cut preserves the bilinear graph and removes the current relaxation point whenever its violation exceeds tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate the four bounded bilinear McCormick inequalities and add those violated by the relaxation point; each preserves the exact bilinear graph.
knowledge_statements.title: Envelope Cut Separation

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Basic Concepts of Global Optimization p. 33

children.title: RLT Cut Separation
children.top_down_role: Separation of cuts derived from reformulation-linearization structures.

assumptions_latex: The node relaxation contains variables \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and lifted variables \(X\in\mathbb S^n\) intended to satisfy \(X=xx^\top\).
Every multiplied linear inequality is valid on the current bounded node domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every returned inequality is valid for lifted feasible points and violated by the current relaxation point beyond tolerance.

notation.meaning: slack of the valid inequality indexed by i
linearization operator replacing each product x_p x_q by X_pq

knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-level RLT separation at one bounded spatial branch-and-cut node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given valid inequalities \(s_i(x)=b_i-a_i^\top x\ge 0\), form selected products \(s_i(x)s_j(x)\ge 0\), including products with bound slacks. Replace every quadratic monomial \(x_p x_q\) by \(X_{pq}\) to obtain the linear RLT inequality \(r_{ij}(x,X):=\mathcal L_X(s_i s_j)\ge 0\). At the relaxation point \((\bar x,\bar X)\), compute \(r_{ij}(\bar x,\bar X)\) over the selected pairs and return each inequality satisfying \(r_{ij}(\bar x,\bar X)<-\tau\), where \(\tau\ge 0\) is the separation tolerance; return none if no such pair exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiply pairs of valid linear slacks, linearize quadratic terms with lifted variables, and add every resulting valid inequality violated beyond the separation tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: RLT Cut Separation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The first-level RLT construction is mathematically plausible and the algorithm kind fits the leaf, but no inspectable source supports the precise lifted formulation and validity claim.

children.title: Combined Separation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Node regimes where envelope cuts and RLT cuts provide complementary strengthening.

assumptions_latex: Envelope and RLT separators return only inequalities valid on the current node domain.
The relaxation is re-solved after each accepted batch of cuts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is either a strengthened valid relaxation or a point with no detected envelope or RLT violation larger than \(\tau\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternating envelope-RLT refinement at a fixed search node.

source_refs.locator: 7.3 Cut and Split (Branch and Bound) Methods p. 176

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(P_0\) as the current lifted node relaxation. For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), solve \(P_k\) and obtain \(z_k\). Generate \(C_k^E=\mathcal S_E(z_k,\tau)\) and \(C_k^R=\mathcal S_R(z_k,\tau)\). After filtering invalid, duplicate, or numerically unacceptable rows, set \(P_{k+1}=P_k\cap\bigcap_{c\in C_k^E\cup C_k^R}c\). Stop when both accepted sets are empty, the iteration limit is reached, or bound improvement is below its prescribed threshold. Output the final relaxation and its bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve the node relaxation, separate envelope and RLT violations, add accepted cuts, and stop when neither family yields a material cut.
knowledge_statements.title: Combined Separation Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: 7.3 Cut and Split (Branch and Bound) Methods p. 176

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited general branch-and-bound section does not specifically support this combined separation algorithm. Moreover, termination by an iteration or bound-improvement limit does not imply absence of envelope or RLT violations, and the role of z_k is not defined precisely.

children.title: Separation Dominance Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural regimes where one separation family subsumes or strengthens another.

assumptions_latex: All compared cuts are valid for the same node-feasible lifted set \(F\).
Each regime starts from the same base relaxation \(P\supseteq F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regime producing the smaller relaxation gives a bound at least as strong for every minimization objective.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-inclusion dominance of valid cut families; computational cost is excluded.

source_refs.locator: 7.3 Cut and Split (Branch and Bound) Methods p. 176

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_E=P\cap E\), \(P_R=P\cap R\), and \(P_{ER}=P\cap E\cap R\), where \(E\) and \(R\) denote the intersections of all accepted envelope and RLT halfspaces. Then \(F\subseteq P_{ER}\subseteq P_E\) and \(F\subseteq P_{ER}\subseteq P_R\). Hence, for every linear minimization objective \(c\), \(\inf_{z\in P_{ER}}c^\top z\ge\max\{\inf_{z\in P_E}c^\top z,\inf_{z\in P_R}c^\top z\}\). Envelope separation dominates RLT separation exactly when \(P_E\subseteq P_R\), with the reverse inclusion characterizing RLT dominance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut regime dominates another when its relaxation is contained in the other; combining both families is never weaker in bound quality.
knowledge_statements.title: Separation Dominance Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: 7.3 Cut and Split (Branch and Bound) Methods p. 176

assumptions_latex: The node-feasible set satisfies a finite disjunction \(F\subseteq\bigcup_{t=1}^m D_t\).
A candidate linear inequality can be validated separately on every disjunct.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An accepted cut is valid for \(F\) and excludes the current relaxation point by more than \(\tau\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic finite-disjunction separation, independent of a particular cut-generating linear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\bar z\) and disjuncts \(D_t\), solve a normalized cut-generating problem for coefficients \((\alpha,\beta)\) subject to \(\alpha^\top z\ge\beta\) for every \(z\in D_t\) and every \(t=1,\ldots,m\). Choose the objective to maximize the normalized violation \(\beta-\alpha^\top\bar z\). If the optimum exceeds \(\tau\ge0\), return \(\alpha^\top z\ge\beta\); otherwise report no cut for the chosen normalization and disjunction. Validity on every disjunct implies validity on their union and therefore on \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimize a normalized inequality valid on every disjunct and return it when it separates the current point beyond tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Disjunctive-Cut Separation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic disjunctive-validity argument is plausible, but no source or sufficiently specified normalization and cut-generating formulation supports the claimed separation algorithm.

children.title: Rank Cut Separation
children.top_down_role: Separation families targeting violations of low-rank structure.

assumptions_latex: The lifted matrix \(Y\in\mathbb S_+^q\) is intended to satisfy \(\operatorname{rank}(Y)\le r\).
A validity oracle is available for the model-specific rank-cut family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A cut is emitted only when validity is certified and its violation at \(\bar Y\) exceeds \(\tau\).

notation.meaning: ordered eigenvalues of the lifted matrix

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral detection followed by model-specific valid rank-cut generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute an eigendecomposition of \(\bar Y\) and the residual \(\rho_r(\bar Y)=\sum_{i=r+1}^q\lambda_i(\bar Y)\). If \(\rho_r(\bar Y)\le\tau_{\rm rank}\), report no detected rank violation. Otherwise use the trailing eigenspace to parameterize candidate inequalities from the prescribed rank-cut family. For each candidate \(a\mathbin{:}Y\le b\), invoke the validity oracle on the node-feasible rank-constrained set and compute \(a\mathbin{:}\bar Y-b\). Return only candidates certified valid with violation exceeding \(\tau\); if none qualify, retain the node for branching or another separator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Detect excess spectral rank, generate model-specific candidate cuts from the trailing eigenspace, and retain only certified, materially violated inequalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank Cut Separation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual test requires an explicit domain such as 0≤r<q, and a trailing eigenspace does not by itself define valid linear rank cuts. The model-specific family and validity oracle require an inspectable source.

children.title: Minor Cut Separation
children.top_down_role: Separation families based on violated matrix-minor relations.

assumptions_latex: The lifted variables satisfy \(X=xx^\top\) at every original feasible point.
Finite node bounds are available for constructing valid envelopes of minor expressions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted minor-derived cut is valid on the node domain and violated by \((\bar x,\bar X)\) beyond tolerance.

notation.meaning: a square submatrix indexed by row set I and column set J

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation from vanishing minors of a rank-one lifted matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For selected index pairs \((I,J)\) with \(|I|=|J|=2\), evaluate \(d_{I,J}=\det(\bar Y_{I,J})\). If \(|d_{I,J}|\le\tau_{\rm minor}\), discard that minor. Otherwise express the identity \(\det(Y_{I,J})=0\) as a bounded bilinear relation and construct its prescribed convex-envelope or disjunctive relaxation on the current node box. Separate \(\bar Y\) from that valid relaxation; return an obtained linear inequality only when its violation exceeds \(\tau\). Report no minor cut when no tested minor yields such an inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Find violated vanishing two-by-two minors, convexify each bounded minor relation, and return valid linear inequalities that materially separate the lifted point.
knowledge_statements.title: Minor Cut Separation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Vanishing 2-by-2 minors are necessary for the intended rank-one lift, but the prescribed bounded convex-envelope or disjunctive construction is not specified or sourced, so validity of the generated linear cuts cannot be reviewed.

children.title: Lifted-Matrix Violation Detection
children.top_down_role: Identification of rank-related violations in lifted matrix relaxations.

assumptions_latex: The intended lifted matrix has the form \(Y=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^\top\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\).
Original feasible lifts satisfy \(Y\succeq0\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(Y)=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The detector classifies \(\bar Y\) as PSD-violating, rank-violating, or numerically consistent with the lifted conditions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eigenvalue-based violation certificate for PSD and rank-one lifted conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Symmetrize the computed matrix and evaluate \(\lambda_{\min}(\bar Y)\) and \(\rho_1(\bar Y)=\operatorname{tr}(\bar Y)-\lambda_{\max}(\bar Y)\). If \(\lambda_{\min}(\bar Y)<-\tau_{\rm psd}\), a corresponding unit eigenvector \(v\) certifies violation through \(v^\top\bar Yv< -\tau_{\rm psd}\). If \(\bar Y\succeq-\tau_{\rm psd}I\) but \(\rho_1(\bar Y)>\tau_{\rm rank}\), the spectrum certifies failure of numerical rank one. Otherwise the matrix is declared consistent only to the specified tolerances, not exactly feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use the smallest eigenvalue to detect PSD failure and the trailing spectral mass to detect failure of numerical rank one.
knowledge_statements.title: Lifted-Matrix Violation Detection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The spectral tests are plausible, but the record describes a detection algorithm rather than a certificate object, and no source supports the particular tolerance-based classification, especially when the matrix is only approximately PSD.

children.title: Numerical Separation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Reliability limits for rank-sensitive or determinant-sensitive cut separation.

assumptions_latex: Eigenvalue and minor residuals are computed in floating-point arithmetic.
All decisions use explicit absolute and relative tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Residuals inside the uncertainty band cannot justify a separating cut or exact rank conclusion without stronger certification.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Floating-point boundary for PSD, rank, and minor separation decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given nonnegative tolerances \(\tau_a,\tau_r,\kappa_a,\kappa_r\), declare definite PSD violation only if \(\lambda_{\min}(Y)<-\eta_{\rm psd}\), and definite rank violation only if \(\rho_r(Y)>\eta_{\rm rank}\). Values satisfying \(|\lambda_{\min}(Y)|\le\eta_{\rm psd}\) or \(|\rho_r(Y)|\le\eta_{\rm rank}\) lie in an uncertainty band. Likewise, a minor residual \(d\) is actionable only when \(|d|\) exceeds its scale-adjusted threshold. Within these bands, cancellation, eigensolver error, or coefficient scaling may reverse the apparent violation, so separation must be withheld or recomputed at higher accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Treat eigenvalue, rank, and minor residuals near scale-adjusted tolerances as numerically unresolved rather than as valid grounds for cutting.
knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Separation Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement does not define r or rho_r locally and does not assume conditions ensuring the trace-scaled rank threshold is nonnegative. The numerical uncertainty policy is implementation-dependent and requires a numerical-analysis source.

children.title: Node Disposition Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Classical branch-and-bound disposition families placed after bounding, reduction, and separation.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Global Optimization: Theory, Algorithms, and Applications
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Fathoming rules
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Global Optimization: Theory, Algorithms, and Applications

assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem with incumbent value \(U\).
The node relaxation supplies a certified lower bound \(L_N\) for every feasible descendant solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(L_N\ge U-\varepsilon\), fathoming node \(N\) preserves \(\varepsilon\)-global optimality.

notation.meaning: certified lower bound at node N
objective value of the current incumbent

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute-gap bound fathoming for minimization.

source_refs.locator: 7.3 Cut and Split (Branch and Bound) Methods p. 176

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_N\) be the original feasible set restricted to node \(N\), and suppose the certified relaxation value satisfies \(L_N\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in F_N\). Let \(U=f(x^I)\) for a globally feasible incumbent \(x^I\), and fix \(\varepsilon\ge0\). If \(L_N\ge U-\varepsilon\), then every \(x\in F_N\) satisfies \(f(x)\ge U-\varepsilon\). Consequently no descendant of \(N\) can improve the incumbent by more than \(\varepsilon\), so the node may be fathomed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discard a minimization node when its certified lower bound cannot improve the incumbent by more than the allowed absolute gap.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Dominance Fathoming

source_witnesses.locator: 7.3 Cut and Split (Branch and Bound) Methods p. 176

assumptions_latex: The infeasibility certificate applies to the node domain and all original constraints.
Certificate arithmetic and any dual bounds used in it are rigorous at the declared tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A valid certificate proving \(F_N=\varnothing\) permits permanent fathoming of node \(N\).

notation.meaning: original feasible set restricted to node N

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node fathoming only from a rigorous infeasibility certificate.

source_refs.locator: 7.3 Cut and Split (Branch and Bound) Methods p. 176

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_N\) denote all points satisfying the original constraints and the branching restrictions of node \(N\). A certificate \(C_N\) is sufficient for infeasibility fathoming when a deterministic verifier establishes that \(C_N\) implies \(F_N=\varnothing\). Permissible forms include a rigorous contradiction from constraint propagation or a valid dual infeasibility certificate for a relaxation whose feasible region contains \(F_N\). A solver status lacking such a verified implication is not sufficient. Once verified, the node and every descendant may be removed from the search.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fathom a node as infeasible only when a checkable certificate proves that no original-feasible point satisfies its branching restrictions.
knowledge_statements.title: Certified-Infeasibility Fathoming

source_witnesses.locator: 7.3 Cut and Split (Branch and Bound) Methods p. 176

assumptions_latex: A node procedure returns a point \(x^N\) satisfying every original constraint within certified feasibility tolerances.
Every designated integer component of \(x^N\) is integral.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The point may update the incumbent; the node is fathomed only if optimality over its domain is also certified.

notation.meaning: original-feasible integral point found at node N
certified lower bound at node N

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Disposition distinguishes incumbent acceptance from node fathoming.

source_refs.locator: 7.3 Cut and Split (Branch and Bound) Methods p. 176

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(x^N\) is feasible for the original nonlinear constraints and integral in every required component, then it is a valid incumbent candidate. For minimization, replace \(U\) by \(f(x^N)\) when \(f(x^N)<U\). Integrality and feasibility alone do not justify fathoming node \(N\): fathoming additionally requires a certificate that no point in the node domain improves the updated incumbent beyond tolerance, for example \(L_N\ge U-\varepsilon\), or a certificate that \(x^N\) is globally optimal over that domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept an original-feasible integral point as an incumbent candidate, but keep the node unless a separate bound or optimality certificate justifies fathoming.
knowledge_statements.title: Integral-Feasible Node Disposition

source_witnesses.locator: 7.3 Cut and Split (Branch and Bound) Methods p. 176

assumptions_latex: A node oracle terminates without a certified bound, feasible solution, or infeasibility conclusion.
No independent fathoming certificate is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The node must remain unresolved and cannot be discarded solely because the oracle failed or stopped.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conservative disposition after numerical, time-limit, or oracle indeterminacy.

source_refs.locator: 7.3 Cut and Split (Branch and Bound) Methods p. 176

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the node oracle returns an indeterminate status, such as a time limit, numerical failure, or an uncertified local conclusion. If this status supplies neither a valid lower bound supporting bound dominance, nor a verified infeasibility certificate, nor a node-optimal feasible solution, then it implies no fathoming predicate. The algorithm must retain \(N\) in \(\mathcal Q\), retry it with altered tolerances or another certified oracle, or branch using independently valid information. Removing \(N\) under the unresolved status alone destroys the global-completeness guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inconclusive oracle result never justifies discarding a node; retain, retry, or branch unless an independent fathoming certificate exists.
knowledge_statements.title: Unresolved-Oracle Node Disposition

source_witnesses.locator: 7.3 Cut and Split (Branch and Bound) Methods p. 176

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Rounding Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic rounding-and-repair family for producing mixed-integer incumbents from node relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a relaxation solution \((\bar x,\bar z)\) with continuous variables \(x\) and integer variables \(z\), choose a finite family \(\mathcal R\) of rounding maps. For each \(R\in\mathcal R\), form \(z^R=R(\bar z)\in Z\), optionally respecting variable bounds and prescribed fixings, and solve or locally search the continuous subproblem \(\min\{f(x,z^R):(x,z^R)\in F\}\). Validate every returned point against the original constraints and objective. Output the validated candidate having the smallest objective value, or report failure if no map yields a feasible candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply several rounding maps to relaxed integer values, optimize or repair the remaining continuous variables, validate all candidates, and return the best feasible incumbent.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times Z\) is the original feasible set.
\((\bar x,\bar z)\) solves or approximates a valid node relaxation.
\(\mathcal R\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\hat y\in F\) is returned only after validation, or the procedure reports failure.

notation.meaning: Integer assignment produced by map R

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: formal synthesis of a standard relaxation-rounding-repair heuristic

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and local scope fit, but no inspectable source supports this synthesized rounding-map family, its repair sequence, or its best-candidate rule for nonconvex MICP.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer-Fixed Local Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal heuristic that fixes discrete variables and locally optimizes the resulting nonconvex continuous problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an integer assignment \(z^0\in Z\), define the fixed-integer subproblem \(P(z^0)=\min\{f(x,z^0):(x,z^0)\in F\}\). Start from a continuous point \(x^0\), optionally obtained from a relaxation or repair step, and apply a local nonlinear solver to \(P(z^0)\). If the solver returns \(x^*\), independently test \((x^*,z^0)\) against the original variable bounds, integrality requirements, and nonlinear constraints. Return it as a primal candidate only when those tests pass; local optimality of \(P(z^0)\) does not establish global optimality of the mixed-integer problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fix an integer assignment, locally solve the remaining nonlinear problem, and accept the result only after validation against the original model.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times Z\) is the original feasible set.
\(z^0\in Z\) satisfies all discrete-domain restrictions.
A local solver is available for \(P(z^0)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A returned point is feasible for the fixed assignment, but need not be globally optimal.

notation.meaning: Continuous nonlinear subproblem at fixed integer assignment

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf and the local-versus-global limitation is appropriate, but the fixed-integer primal heuristic has no cited source or locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Guided Primal Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses relaxation values and dual information to prioritize discrete assignments and continuous starts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a search node, solve a valid relaxation and obtain a primal relaxation point \((\bar x,\bar z)\), with optional reduced costs or constraint multipliers. Construct a finite ordered set \(S\subseteq Z\) of integer assignments by favoring values near \(\bar z\) and variables indicated as influential by the relaxation information. For each \(z\in S\), initialize a local or repair solve from \(\bar x\), seek a point in \(F\) with integer part \(z\), and validate any returned point. Stop at a prescribed work limit or after exhausting \(S\); output the best validated candidate found.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use relaxation values and sensitivity information to prioritize integer assignments, launch local or repair solves, and retain the best validated feasible point.
assumptions_latex: The node relaxation is valid for the node region.
The ordered candidate set \(S\) is finite.
Every proposed incumbent is checked against the original model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is the best validated point generated from \(S\), or failure if none is feasible.

notation.meaning: Ordered set of candidate integer assignments

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: formal abstraction of relaxation-guided primal heuristics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but the proposed use of reduced costs or multipliers to order integer assignments is an unspecified heuristic synthesis without supporting evidence.

children.title: Incumbent Feasibility Validation
children.top_down_role: Validation of candidate incumbents against original discrete, nonlinear, and conic requirements.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Feasibility Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tolerance-aware certificate for accepting a proposed mixed-integer point as feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a candidate \(y=(x,z)\), recompute all original-model expressions and define \(v_b(y)\) as the maximum bound violation, \(v_i(y)=\max_j\operatorname{dist}(z_j,Z_j)\), \(v_g(y)=\max_k[g_k(y)]_+\), and \(v_h(y)=\max_\ell|h_\ell(y)|\). Given nonnegative tolerances \(\tau_b,\tau_i,\tau_g,\tau_h\), the validation certificate is the recorded tuple of recomputed residuals and data provenance. The candidate passes precisely when every residual is finite and \(v_b(y)\le\tau_b\), \(v_i(y)\le\tau_i\), \(v_g(y)\le\tau_g\), and \(v_h(y)\le\tau_h\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recompute original bounds, integrality, inequalities, and equalities; accept the candidate exactly when every finite residual lies within its declared tolerance.
assumptions_latex: All constraints are evaluated using the original model data.
Validation tolerances are fixed and nonnegative.
Undefined or nonfinite evaluations count as failure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The residual tuple certifies tolerance-feasibility exactly when all four displayed tests pass.

notation.meaning: Bound, integrality, inequality, and equality violations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits feasibility validation, but the residual definitions and tolerance-based acceptance semantics are solver-numerics policy claims requiring a specific source.

children.title: Incumbent Objective Validation
children.top_down_role: Validation of the objective value attached to a candidate incumbent.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Objective Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent recomputation and comparison of a candidate objective before incumbent replacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a feasibility-validated candidate \(y\), independently evaluate the original objective to obtain \(\hat f(y)\). Reject the objective certificate if evaluation is nonfinite or if \(|\hat f(y)-f_{\mathrm{reported}}(y)|>\tau_f\max\{1,|\hat f(y)|\}\). For minimization with current incumbent value \(U\), certify strict improvement only when \(\hat f(y)<U-\tau_U\max\{1,|U|\}\), where \(\tau_f,\tau_U\ge0\). The certificate records \(y\), both objective values, tolerances, model version, and arithmetic status; only \(\hat f(y)\) may update \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recompute the original objective, reconcile it with the reported value, and replace a minimization incumbent only after a tolerance-significant improvement.
assumptions_latex: The candidate has passed feasibility validation.
The problem is stated as minimization.
Objective and incumbent tolerances are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The incumbent bound updates to \(\hat f(y)\) only if objective consistency and strict-improvement tests both pass.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits, but the relative discrepancy and incumbent-improvement tests are particular numerical policies with no cited authority.

children.title: Incumbent Repair Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Mechanisms for recovering acceptable candidates from nearly feasible primal points.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Repair Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection, restoration, or penalty-based repair of a nearly feasible mixed-integer candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a candidate \(y^0=(x^0,z^0)\), first map its integer component to an admissible assignment \(z^r\in Z\), respecting node fixings. Then solve a bounded restoration problem \(\min_x V(x,z^r)+\rho d((x,z^r),y^0)\), where \(V\ge0\) aggregates original-model constraint violations, \(d\ge0\) limits displacement, and \(\rho\ge0\). Terminate at a work limit, infeasibility declaration, or candidate \(y^r=(x^r,z^r)\). Recompute original residuals and objective; output \(y^r\) only if the separate feasibility and objective validation rules pass.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repair integrality, minimize original constraint violation while limiting displacement, then accept only a separately validated feasible candidate and objective.
assumptions_latex: The repair preserves all active node fixings.
\(V(y)=0\) exactly for original-model feasibility within zero tolerance.
Repair effort has a finite prescribed limit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A repaired point enters incumbent comparison only after independent feasibility and objective validation.

notation.meaning: Displacement measure from the proposed point

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but the stated restoration objective, integer-mapping step, and validation sequence combine multiple repair variants without evidence for this exact formulation.

children.title: Repair Acceptance Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Certification limits governing whether a repaired point may update the incumbent.

knowledge_statements.title: Repair Acceptance Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary acceptance predicate separating successful repair from merely reduced infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y^0\) be the proposed point and \(y^r\) its repaired version. Accept \(y^r\) for incumbent comparison if and only if: it respects every active node fixing; all recomputed original-model residuals satisfy their declared tolerances; its objective evaluation is finite and validated; and the repair budget constraints \(d(y^r,y^0)\le\Delta\) and \(W(y^r)\le B\) hold whenever displacement limit \(\Delta\) and work limit \(B\) are imposed. A reduction in aggregate violation without satisfaction of these conditions is not sufficient for acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept repair only when fixings, feasibility, objective validity, displacement, and work limits all pass; reduced violation alone is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: \(\Delta\ge0\) is the allowed repair displacement when imposed.
\(B\ge0\) is the allowed repair work when imposed.
Residual and objective tolerances are fixed before validation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y^r\) is admissible for incumbent comparison exactly when the complete acceptance predicate holds.

notation.meaning: Work consumed in producing the repair

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the leaf, but displacement and work limits are optional implementation policies rather than established necessary acceptance conditions; a source defining the intended regime is required.

children.title: Tree-Oracle Coordination
children.top_down_role: Implementation mechanisms specific to coordinating the global tree with conic relaxation engines.

knowledge_statements.title: Node-Selection Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unified priority-rule representation of best-bound, depth-first, breadth-first, and hybrid tree search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a finite active-node set \(Q\). At each iteration select \(N\in\arg\min_{M\in Q}\pi(M;s)\), remove \(N\) from \(Q\), process its relaxation and branching operations, and insert every surviving child. The score \(\pi\) may encode best-bound search, depth-first search, breadth-first search, or a state-dependent hybrid; deterministic tie-breaking completes the rule. Prune nodes only through valid infeasibility, dominance, or bound tests. Stop when \(Q=\varnothing\), a certified global gap tolerance is met, or an explicit resource limit is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select active nodes by a declared priority score encompassing best-bound, depth-first, breadth-first, or hybrid search, with deterministic ties and valid pruning.
assumptions_latex: The active-node set \(Q\) is finite at each iteration.
Each node carries a valid relaxation bound.
Pruning tests preserve every globally improving feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rule determines the next processed node without changing the validity of bounds or pruning certificates.

notation.meaning: Node priority score under search state s

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, and the priority-score abstraction is plausible, but no branch-and-bound or nonconvex MICP source supports the stated family and stopping conditions.

knowledge_statements.title: Conic Relaxation Warm Starts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfers compatible primal-dual conic states between related spatial-search nodes without weakening validity checks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a child conic relaxation derived from a parent, map the parent state \((x_p,s_p,y_p)\) into the child's variable, slack, and dual spaces. Project or regularize the mapped primal slack into the child's cone and discard dual components associated with removed constraints; initialize new constraints with solver-admissible values. Before use, check dimensions, cone membership required by the solver, and consistency with child bounds. Run the conic solver from this state, but determine feasibility, bound validity, and termination solely from the child's relaxation and certified solver outputs; otherwise restart cold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Map a parent primal-dual conic state to a child, repair compatibility, and use it only as initialization while certifying results from the child relaxation.
assumptions_latex: Parent and child conic formulations have a known variable-and-constraint correspondence.
The warm start does not alter the child relaxation.
The conic solver accepts external initialization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Warm starting may change computational effort but not the mathematical validity criterion for the child bound.

notation.meaning: Parent primal variable, conic slack, and dual state

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but conic warm-start admissibility is solver- and formulation-dependent. No source supports this protocol, and the listed cone symbol K is not used in the statement.

children.title: Cut Aging Policies
children.top_down_role: Cut-retention policies based on age, activity, or historical contribution.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Aging Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Activity-based lifecycle rule for removable relaxation cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assign each removable cut \(c\) an age \(a_c=0\) when inserted. After each eligible relaxation solve, reset \(a_c\leftarrow0\) if its slack is at most \(\tau_c\) or its dual activity exceeds \(\eta_c\); otherwise set \(a_c\leftarrow a_c+1\). Delete or deactivate \(c\) when \(a_c>A_c\), unless it is protected by validity-critical status, recent efficacy, or an active descendant-locality requirement. Deletion changes only the current relaxation representation: the cut may be regenerated, and every retained or regenerated cut must remain valid on its declared domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increase a cut's age while inactive, reset it when active, and remove it past a threshold unless protected by validity or locality requirements.
assumptions_latex: Each managed cut has a declared validity domain.
\(\tau_c,\eta_c,A_c\) are fixed policy parameters.
Mandatory model constraints are not removable cuts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only unprotected cuts older than their thresholds are eligible for deletion or deactivation.

notation.meaning: Current inactivity age of cut c

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard activity-based cut aging policy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but the precise slack/dual-activity aging rule, protections, and deletion threshold are implementation-specific and uncited.

children.title: Cut Locality Tracking
children.top_down_role: Tracking of node domains and subtrees where stored cuts remain valid.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Locality Tracking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain metadata determining where a spatially valid cut may be installed or reused.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent a cut \(c\) by \((\alpha_c,\beta_c,D_c,o_c)\), where \(\alpha_c^Ty\le\beta_c\) is its linear inequality, \(D_c\) is the region on which validity was established, and \(o_c\) is its origin node. The cut is eligible at node \(N\), with node region \(D_N\), only if \(D_N\subseteq D_c\). A globally valid cut has \(D_c=D_{\mathrm{root}}\); a local cut is inherited only by descendants whose regions remain within \(D_c\). Moving a local cut outside this containment relation is forbidden unless global validity is separately certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Store each cut's inequality, validity region, and origin; install it at a node only when that node's region lies within the cut's validity region.
assumptions_latex: Each search node has a well-defined region \(D_N\).
Every cut has a recorded validity region \(D_c\).
Child-node regions are subsets of their parent regions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The containment test \(D_N\subseteq D_c\) is necessary for locality-safe cut reuse.

notation.meaning: Certified validity region of cut c

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: validity-domain representation for local cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits, and domain containment is mathematically plausible, but the exact locality metadata and reuse criterion lack a spatial branch-and-cut source.

children.title: Age–Locality Retention Regimes
children.top_down_role: Retention regimes balancing cut age against locality-sensitive reuse.

knowledge_statements.title: Age–Locality Retention Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint retention predicate combining inactivity age with a cut's remaining descendant scope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For cut \(c\) at node \(N\), let \(a_c\) be its inactivity age, \(A_c\) its deletion threshold, and \(L_c(N)\) the set of open nodes below \(N\) whose regions lie within the validity region \(D_c\). Retain \(c\) whenever \(a_c\le A_c\), or whenever \(L_c(N)\ne\varnothing\) and regeneration cost or policy marks it protected. Delete an unprotected cut only when \(a_c>A_c\) and either \(L_c(N)=\varnothing\) or the cut is stored for safe regeneration in every eligible descendant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retain young cuts and protected cuts still relevant to open descendants; delete old cuts only when locality obligations vanish or safe regeneration is guaranteed.
assumptions_latex: Cut locality metadata are correct.
Open-node membership is updated as the tree changes.
Deletion never removes an original model constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Age alone is insufficient for deletion while an unserved eligible descendant remains.

notation.meaning: Open eligible descendants for cut c below node N

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conservative synthesis of age and locality retention

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits, but the joint age-locality predicate is a synthesized cut-management policy. Its protection and regeneration conditions require a specific supporting source.

children.title: Premature-Deletion Risks
children.top_down_role: Search degradation risks caused by discarding still-useful global or local cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Premature-Deletion Risks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes correctness-preserving cut removal from deletion that breaks progress or retained certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a minimization branch-and-cut method. Removing a valid cut from a node relaxation and recomputing the node bound can only weaken that relaxation; therefore it does not by itself create an invalid lower bound. Premature deletion becomes unsafe when the algorithm retains a pruning decision or bound whose recorded certificate requires the deleted cut but neither archives the cut nor independently verifies the certificate. It can also defeat finite progress: if a repeatedly violated cut is deleted before it becomes active at all relevant nodes, the search may regenerate the same cut indefinitely. Thus deletion is admissible only after every dependent certificate is preserved or revalidated and the cut-aging policy prevents infinite delete–regenerate cycles.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting a valid cut is safe after recomputation, but can destroy auditable pruning certificates or cause endless cut regeneration unless dependencies and aging are controlled.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem solved by spatial branch-and-cut.
Every pruning decision must have a verifiable lower-bound or infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Cut deletion is correctness-safe only when dependent certificates remain valid, and convergence-safe only when infinite delete–regenerate cycling is excluded.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: removing constraints weakens a minimization relaxation, while certificate retention and finite-progress requirements follow from branch-and-cut invariants

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits, but the assertions about retained pruning certificates and exclusion of infinite delete–regenerate cycles require a specialized cut-management or branch-and-cut convergence source.

children.title: Parallel Tree Coordination
children.top_down_role: Coordination of concurrent node exploration across global-search workers.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Tree Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shared-memory or distributed coordination of a spatial branch-and-bound tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a root node and a valid node-bounding routine. Initialize a concurrent queue with the root and set the incumbent value to \(+\infty\). Each worker atomically claims one node, constructs its valid relaxation, and obtains a lower bound or an infeasibility certificate. It discards the node only if certified infeasible or if its lower bound is no smaller than the current verified incumbent; otherwise it branches into children whose domains collectively contain every feasible point retained from the parent and atomically inserts those children. Feasible solutions update the incumbent by atomic minimum. Output the incumbent only after a termination detector confirms that the queue is empty and no worker owns an unreported node or pending child.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers atomically claim, bound, branch, and enqueue nodes; branching must preserve every unpruned feasible point, and global termination requires both an empty queue and no active or unreported work.
assumptions_latex: Every node relaxation contains all feasible points in that node domain.
Every branching operation produces child domains whose union contains every feasible point of the parent not otherwise certified prunable.
Every incumbent update comes from a verified feasible point.
Queue ownership and incumbent updates are atomic or serializable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns the best verified incumbent only after all nodes capable of improving it have been certified processed or pruned.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: work ownership, feasible-region coverage, and termination detection are necessary parallel branch-and-bound invariants

children.title: Parallel Oracle Coordination
children.top_down_role: Coordination of concurrent conic relaxation or certificate-oracle workloads.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Oracle Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinates concurrent relaxation, separation, propagation, and bounding oracle calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each oracle request, transmit a node identifier, its domain description, a model revision, and the assumptions under which the result is valid. An oracle returns a bound, cut, reduction, or infeasibility certificate together with the same tags and its validity domain. Before incorporation, a coordinator verifies the certificate and checks that the current node domain is contained in the reported validity domain and that the model revision and assumptions remain compatible. Accepted global results enter the shared pool; accepted local results are attached only to eligible nodes. Rejected or unverifiable results may guide scheduling but cannot justify pruning, domain reduction, or global termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallel oracle results must carry domain and model tags; only verified, scope-compatible results may alter bounds, domains, pruning, or termination.
assumptions_latex: Every oracle result exposes a checkable validity scope.
Node and model revisions are uniquely identifiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only verified oracle results whose validity scope covers the receiving node may affect correctness-critical search state.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: tagged requests and scope validation enforce the usual locality invariant for asynchronous solver components

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm and container match, but the proposed revision-tagging, scope-verification, shared-pool, and heuristic-use protocol is specialized and has no inspectable source.

children.title: Asynchronous Bound Exchange
children.top_down_role: Exchange of qualified lower bounds and incumbent information across asynchronous workers.

knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Bound Exchange
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone exchange of certified lower and upper bounds among asynchronous workers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization, each worker maintains a certified lower bound \(L_v\) for every owned node \(v\) and a verified incumbent upper bound \(U\). Messages merge by \(L_v\leftarrow\max\{L_v,L_v^{\mathrm{msg}}\}\) only when the received bound is certified for the current node domain, and by \(U\leftarrow\min\{U,U^{\mathrm{msg}}\}\) only when the message identifies a verified feasible solution. A worker may prune \(v\) when \(L_v\ge U-\varepsilon\). Stale but valid messages can delay pruning but cannot make this test unsound. Global termination additionally requires a consistent snapshot or termination protocol accounting for all in-transit bound and work messages.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified bounds merge monotonically; stale valid messages only delay progress, while termination must account for active workers and messages in transit.
assumptions_latex: The requested absolute optimality tolerance satisfies \(\varepsilon\ge 0\).
All exchanged lower bounds and incumbents retain verifiable certificates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The asynchronous pruning test \(L_v\ge U-\varepsilon\) is safe, but termination requires detection of quiescence including messages in transit.

notation.meaning: certified lower bound for node v

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: max-merging lower bounds and min-merging feasible upper bounds preserve minimization-bound validity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The monotone bound updates are mathematically plausible, but the asynchronous safety and consistent-snapshot termination claims require a source addressing delayed messages and distributed termination.

children.title: Stale-Certificate Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Validity limits for certificates or cuts produced from outdated node domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Stale-Certificate Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies when delayed certificates cease to justify correctness-critical decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A delayed certificate remains usable only if its conclusion is valid for the current model and node domain. Validity is preserved when the current feasible node set lies within the certificate's validity domain and no model revision has invalidated an assumption used by the certificate. It is not preserved merely because the node identifier is unchanged. In particular, a local cut certificate cannot be exported to an unrelated node, a bound cannot qualify a revised model when the revision invalidates an assumption supporting that bound, and an unverified incumbent cannot support pruning. Outside these boundaries, a stale result may be retained as heuristic information but must not certify pruning, infeasibility, domain reduction, or termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stale certificate is authoritative only while the current node and model satisfy its recorded validity conditions; otherwise it is heuristic information.
assumptions_latex: Certificates record their model revision, assumptions, and validity domain.
Correctness-critical decisions require currently valid certificates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A stale certificate may justify a decision only when the present model and node domain satisfy its recorded validity conditions.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: certificate validity is conditional on the assumptions and domain under which the certificate was derived

children.title: Global MICP Guarantee Frontier
children.top_down_role: Guarantee families ordered from validity of individual bounds through search convergence and composite gap certificates to complexity frontiers.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Global Optimization: Theory, Algorithms, and Applications
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Complexity; branch-and-bound convergence and finiteness
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Global Optimization: Theory, Algorithms, and Applications

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Handbook of Global Optimization
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Conditions for global optimality; complexity issues; successive partitioning; DC duality
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Handbook of Global Optimization

knowledge_statements.title: Global Relaxation Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-inclusion condition for a globally valid minimization relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq X\) be the feasible set of a minimization problem with objective \(f:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\). A set \(R\subseteq X\) is a globally valid relaxation precisely when \(F\subseteq R\). Its relaxation value \(L=\inf\{f(x):x\in R\}\) then satisfies \(L\le \,\inf\{f(x):x\in F\}\). Consequently, certified infeasibility of \(R\) certifies infeasibility of \(F\), and a finite relaxation value is a valid global lower bound. Constraint transformations used to construct \(R\) must preserve the inclusion \(F\subseteq R\); objective underestimators require the analogous pointwise inequality on the retained domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global relaxation contains every feasible point, so its minimum is a valid global lower bound and its infeasibility proves original infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: The optimization problem is \(\inf\{f(x):x\in F\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(F\subseteq R\), then \(\inf_{x\in R}f(x)\le\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\).

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Basic Concepts of Global Optimization p. 33

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Basic Concepts of Global Optimization p. 33

knowledge_statements.title: Node-Local Relaxation Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity condition for a relaxation restricted to one search-tree node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let node \(v\) have domain \(D_v\subseteq X\), and let \(F\subseteq X\) be the original feasible set. A node relaxation \(R_v\subseteq X\) is valid at \(v\) when \(F\cap D_v\subseteq R_v\). For minimization with objective \(f\), the value \(L_v=\inf\{f(x):x\in R_v\}\) is then a lower bound on \(\inf\{f(x):x\in F\cap D_v\}\). This condition is local: it supplies no bound for feasible points outside \(D_v\). Every cut, domain reduction, and objective underestimator used in \(R_v\) must therefore be valid on all of \(F\cap D_v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node relaxation must contain every feasible point in that node; its value bounds only that node's restricted optimization problem.
assumptions_latex: The problem minimizes \(f:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) over \(F\).
Node \(v\) represents the domain \(D_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(F\cap D_v\subseteq R_v\), then \(L_v\le\inf_{x\in F\cap D_v}f(x)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: restricting the global relaxation inclusion and lower-bound argument to a node domain yields the stated condition

children.title: Global Cut Inheritance
children.top_down_role: Inheritance behavior for cuts valid throughout the global feasible domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Cut Inheritance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inheritance rule for cuts valid on the entire original feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the original feasible set, and suppose the inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) is globally valid, meaning \(F\subseteq\{x:a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\}\). For every search node \(v\) with domain \(D_v\), one has \(F\cap D_v\subseteq\{x:a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\}\). Hence the cut may be inserted into the relaxation of every existing or future node without changing its locality tag. Its inheritance remains valid under branching, propagation, and domain contraction, provided the original model and the meaning of \(F\) have not changed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut valid for the entire feasible set is valid at every node and remains inheritable under domain restriction.
assumptions_latex: The inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) is valid for every \(x\in F\).
All tree nodes represent restrictions of the same feasible model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every node \(v\), the cut is valid on \(F\cap D_v\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: intersection with any node domain preserves validity of an inequality holding on the full feasible set

children.title: Descendant-Node Cut Inheritance
children.top_down_role: Inheritance behavior for local cuts within qualified descendant-node domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Descendant-Node Cut Inheritance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inheritance of a locally valid cut along nested descendant domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a cut \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) be valid for the feasible portion \(F\cap D_v\) of node \(v\). If node \(w\) is a descendant of \(v\) and branching or propagation ensures \(D_w\subseteq D_v\), then \(F\cap D_w\subseteq F\cap D_v\). Therefore the cut is valid at \(w\) and may be inherited by every such descendant. This rule does not authorize transfer to a sibling, ancestor, or node whose domain is not contained in \(D_v\), even if the receiving node shares some branching assignments with \(v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node-local cut passes safely to descendants whose domains are contained in the cut's validity domain, but not automatically elsewhere.
assumptions_latex: The cut is valid on \(F\cap D_v\).
The descendant domain satisfies \(D_w\subseteq D_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cut is valid on \(F\cap D_w\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: set containment transfers validity from an origin node to every nested descendant domain

children.title: Locality-Domain Tracking
children.top_down_role: Representation of the domain restrictions attached to locally valid cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Locality-Domain Tracking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metadata representation for determining where each local cut may be applied.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent each cut \(c: a_c^{\mathsf T}x\le b_c\) by a locality record \((\mathcal L_c,r_c,A_c)\), where \(\mathcal L_c\subseteq X\) is a certified validity domain, \(r_c\) is the model revision, and \(A_c\) records assumptions used by its certificate. The defining validity condition is \(F_{r_c}\cap\mathcal L_c\subseteq\{x:a_c^{\mathsf T}x\le b_c\}\). At a current node \(v\), the cut is admissible only after verifying revision compatibility, assumption compatibility, and \(F\cap D_v\subseteq\mathcal L_c\). A global cut uses \(\mathcal L_c=X\); a node-local cut may use its origin domain or another explicitly certified region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each cut carries a validity domain, model revision, and assumptions; it is applied only where current feasible node points lie within that scope.
assumptions_latex: Every cut certificate identifies a validity domain and model revision.
Current node domains and model revisions are available to the verifier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Cut \(c\) is eligible at node \(v\) only when its recorded validity conditions cover \(F\cap D_v\).

notation.meaning: certified validity domain of cut c
model revision under which cut c was certified

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit validity-domain metadata operationalizes global and descendant cut-inheritance conditions

children.title: Invalid Inheritance Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Tree transitions across which a local cut may no longer be inherited safely.

knowledge_statements.title: Invalid Inheritance Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete counterexample to inheritance without containment of validity domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\mathbb Z\), let an origin node have domain \(D_v=\{x\in\mathbb R:x\le 0\}\), and use the local cut \(x\le 0\). The cut is valid on \(F\cap D_v\). Its integer-branching sibling can have domain \(D_w=\{x\in\mathbb R:x\ge 1\}\); that node contains the feasible point \(x=1\), which violates the cut. Thus local validity at \(v\) does not imply validity at a node \(w\) lacking \(D_w\subseteq D_v\). More generally, inheritance is invalid whenever the receiving node contains a feasible point outside the recorded validity domain that violates the cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For integer-feasible x, the cut x ≤ 0 is valid on node x ≤ 0 but invalid on its sibling x ≥ 1, showing that locality cannot cross nonnested domains.
assumptions_latex: Local cuts are certified only on their recorded origin or validity domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Node-local cut inheritance can fail whenever the receiving domain is not contained in the cut's validity domain.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the displayed one-dimensional integer instance directly establishes the failure mechanism
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle-Bound Qualification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate requirements for accepting an oracle value as a node lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For node domain \(D_v\), an oracle lower-bound certificate consists of a relaxation \(Q_v\), a value \(L_v\), and verifiable data establishing \(F\cap D_v\subseteq Q_v\) and \(L_v\le\inf\{f(x):x\in Q_v\}\). These relations imply \(L_v\le\inf\{f(x):x\in F\cap D_v\}\), so \(L_v\) may qualify pruning or a global gap computation. The certificate must also identify its node domain, model revision, tolerances, and any local cuts or objective underestimators used. A numerical value without these validity checks is an estimate, not a qualified bound, and cannot support correctness-critical decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An oracle value qualifies as a lower bound only with verifiable relaxation containment, objective certification, domain scope, revision, and tolerance metadata.
assumptions_latex: The problem minimizes \(f\) over feasible set \(F\).
Node \(v\) represents domain \(D_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A verified certificate yields \(L_v\le\inf_{x\in F\cap D_v}f(x)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Exhaustive-Partition Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines spatial exhaustiveness along every infinite branch of a nested finite partition tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X^0\subset\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \((\mathcal{P}_k)_{k\geq0}\) be nested finite partitions of \(X^0\). The sequence is exhaustive if, for every nested sequence \(Q_0\supseteq Q_1\supseteq\cdots\) satisfying \(Q_k\in\mathcal{P}_k\) for every \(k\), one has \(\operatorname{diam}(Q_k)\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nested finite partition sequence is exhaustive when the regions on every infinite branch have diameters converging to zero.

Every refinement replaces a box by finitely many boxes whose union equals the parent box.

knowledge_statements.title: Consistent-Bounding Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines pointwise consistency of fixed-integer node bounds on shrinking spatial regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{Z}^p\) be the feasible set and let \(f:F\to\mathbb{R}\). A node-bounding rule \(L(Q,z)\) is consistent if it is valid for every spatial region \(Q\subseteq X^0\) and admissible integer assignment \(z\), and if, for every nested sequence \(Q_j\downarrow\{\bar x\}\), \((\bar x,\bar z)\in F\) implies \(L(Q_j,\bar z)\to f(\bar x,\bar z)\). If \((\bar x,\bar z)\notin F\) and a neighborhood of \((\bar x,\bar z)\) contains no feasible point with integer assignment \(\bar z\), consistency additionally requires eventual certified infeasibility of \((Q_j,\bar z)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A consistent fixed-integer node bound is valid and becomes exact on regions shrinking to a feasible point; robustly infeasible limit points are eventually certified infeasible.
assumptions_latex: The feasible set is \(F\subseteq X^0\times\mathbb{Z}^p\), where \(X^0\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is compact.
For every \(Q\subseteq X^0\) and admissible \(z\), \(L(Q,z)\) is a valid lower bound for the original problem restricted to \(Q\times\{z\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(Q_j\downarrow\{\bar x\}\) and \((\bar x,\bar z)\in F\), then \(L(Q_j,\bar z)\to f(\bar x,\bar z)\); robust fixed-integer infeasibility is eventually certified.

knowledge_statements.title: Asymptotic Global Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic convergence theorem for fair spatial branch-and-bound with attainable incumbents.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a minimization algorithm for a nonempty compact feasible set with continuous objective and optimal value \(v^*\). At iteration \(k\), let \(L_k\) be a valid global lower bound and let \(U_k\) be the best feasible incumbent value found through iteration \(k\). Suppose the algorithm uses exhaustive partitioning and consistent node bounds, never discards a node that can contain a solution better than the incumbent without a valid certificate, fairly processes every indefinitely competitive node, and generates feasible incumbents arbitrarily close to every feasible limit point of an infinite competitive branch. Then \(\lim_{k\to\infty}L_k=v^*\), \(\lim_{k\to\infty}U_k=v^*\), and every accumulation point of the incumbent solutions is globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under exhaustive refinement, consistent bounds, fair processing, valid fathoming, and adequate incumbent generation, the global lower and incumbent bounds converge to the MICP optimum.
assumptions_latex: The feasible region is nonempty and compact, and the objective is continuous.
The partition rule is exhaustive and the node lower bounds are consistent.
Fathoming is valid, node processing is fair for indefinitely competitive nodes, and feasible incumbents are generated arbitrarily close to feasible limit points of infinite competitive branches.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lim_{k\to\infty}L_k=v^*\), \(\lim_{k\to\infty}U_k=v^*\), and every accumulation point of the incumbent solutions is globally optimal.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Tolerance Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination at a positive absolute tolerance, not exact zero-gap termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\) be the minimum valid lower bound over the active nodes and let \(U\) be the best feasible incumbent value. Fix \(\varepsilon>0\). Suppose there is \(\delta(\varepsilon)>0\) such that processing any node of diameter at most \(\delta(\varepsilon)\) finitely produces either a valid infeasibility certificate or a feasible local incumbent whose value is at most \(\varepsilon\) above that node's valid lower bound. If branching is finite and exhaustive, fathoming is valid, and every unresolved node is eventually processed, then the algorithm reaches \(U-L\leq\varepsilon\) after finitely many node computations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every sufficiently small node is finitely resolved with a valid local gap certificate, exhaustive finite branching and fair processing terminate at every positive absolute tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The initial search domain is compact, branching has finitely many children, and the partition rule is exhaustive.

knowledge_statements.title: Conic Lower-Bound Component
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-feasible conic certificate for a node lower bound in minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization node \(Q\), let \(C_Q\) be a lifted conic relaxation containing the lift of every original feasible point whose spatial coordinates lie in \(Q\), and define \(L_Q:=\inf\{\langle c,w\rangle:w\in C_Q\}\). If \(v_Q^*\) is the original optimal value restricted to \(Q\), then \(L_Q\leq v_Q^*\). For every feasible point \(y\) of the associated conic dual, weak conic duality gives \(d_Q(y)\leq L_Q\leq v_Q^*\), so \(d_Q(y)\) is an independently checkable node lower-bound certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conic relaxation gives a node lower bound, and any associated dual-feasible point gives a directly checkable, possibly weaker lower-bound certificate.
assumptions_latex: The lifted conic relaxation contains the lift of every original feasible point in the node region.
The conic primal and associated dual use a valid cone and dual-cone pairing.

children.title: Absolute Gap Regime
children.top_down_role: Certification cases governed by an absolute difference between incumbent values and valid lower bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Absolute Gap Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-independent additive gap convention for finite minimization bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given finite valid bounds \(L\leq v^*\leq U\) for a minimization problem, define the absolute certified gap by \(g_{\mathrm{abs}}:=U-L\). For a tolerance \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\geq0\), the absolute-gap regime declares the incumbent \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\)-globally optimal when \(g_{\mathrm{abs}}\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\); this condition certifies \(U-v^*\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\). The tolerance has the same units as the objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The absolute regime stops when the upper bound minus the lower bound is at most the chosen additive tolerance, thereby bounding incumbent suboptimality.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem with finite valid bounds \(L\leq v^*\leq U\).
The requested absolute tolerance satisfies \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U-L\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\Longrightarrow U-v^*\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\).

children.title: Relative Gap Regime
children.top_down_role: Certification cases governed by scale-normalized separation between incumbent values and valid lower bounds.

assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem with finite valid bounds \(L\leq v^*\leq U\).
A strictly positive reference scale \(r(U,L)>0\) and tolerance \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\geq0\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\dfrac{U-L}{r(U,L)}\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\Longrightarrow U-v^*\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}r(U,L)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative-gap definition parameterized by an explicitly declared positive reference scale.

source_refs.locator: 3.6 Finite epsilon-Convergence and epsilon-Global Optimality p. 87

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite valid bounds \(L\leq v^*\leq U\), fix and report a reference rule \(r(U,L)>0\), and define \(g_{\mathrm{rel}}:=(U-L)/r(U,L)\). The relative-gap regime declares termination when \(g_{\mathrm{rel}}\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\), which certifies \(U-v^*\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}r(U,L)\). Common choices include \(r(U,L)=|U|\) when \(U\neq0\) and the safeguarded scale \(r(U,L)=\max\{1,|U|,|L|\}\). Because these conventions give different numerical gaps, the reference rule is part of the certificate and cannot be omitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relative gap divides the certified absolute gap by a declared positive scale; the certificate must state the denominator convention.
knowledge_statements.title: Relative Gap Regime

source_witnesses.locator: 3.6 Finite epsilon-Convergence and epsilon-Global Optimality p. 87

children.title: Zero-Reference Gap Regime
children.top_down_role: Reference-value cases where ordinary relative-gap interpretation becomes unavailable or unstable.

assumptions_latex: The relative-gap convention uses a reference value \(r(U,L)\) that may equal zero.
The bounds are finite and satisfy \(L\leq v^*\leq U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r(U,L)=0\Longrightarrow\bigl(U=L\ \text{or an absolute or safeguarded gap rule is required}\bigr)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary case where an unsafeguarded relative-gap denominator vanishes.

source_refs.locator: 3.6 Finite epsilon-Convergence and epsilon-Global Optimality p. 87

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a relative-gap rule uses a reference \(r(U,L)\) that vanishes, the quotient \((U-L)/r(U,L)\) is undefined whenever \(U>L\) and is indeterminate when \(U=L\). Therefore a zero-reference certificate must either establish \(U=L\), apply an absolute-gap test \(U-L\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\), or replace the denominator by a declared safeguard such as \(\max\{\sigma,|U|,|L|\}\) with \(\sigma>0\). Reporting a finite unsafeguarded relative gap from a zero denominator does not certify any bound on incumbent suboptimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the relative-gap reference is zero, division gives no certificate unless the bounds coincide or an absolute or safeguarded rule is used.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Reference Gap Regime

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Partition Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination through a finite spatial partition whose non-infeasible cells have certified local gaps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonempty minimization problem is in a finite partition regime at tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\) if its spatial domain has a finite partition \(\mathcal{P}=\{Q_1,\ldots,Q_m\}\) and every cell can be processed finitely to yield either a valid infeasibility certificate or finite valid local bounds \(L_i\leq v_i\leq U_i\) satisfying \(U_i-L_i\leq\varepsilon\). Let \(I\) be the nonempty set of indices of cells not certified infeasible. After all cells are processed, \(L:=\min_{i\in I}L_i\) and \(U:=\min_{i\in I}U_i\) satisfy \(L\leq v^*\leq U\) and \(U-L\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite partition whose non-infeasible cells are finitely certified to the requested local tolerance yields a finite global gap certificate.

Every cell is processed finitely and yields either certified infeasibility or finite valid bounds \(L_i\leq v_i\leq U_i\).
